dishes.name: Com Trang (Steamed Jasmine Rice)

ingredients: 400 g Vietnamese jasmine rice (gao thom, e.g. ST25 or Thai hom mali)
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cool water, swirling and draining 2–3 times until the water runs almost clear.
Put the rice and water in a rice cooker or heavy pot; the water should sit about one finger joint above the rice.
If using a pot, bring to a boil over medium-high heat uncovered, then cover, turn to the lowest heat and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and rest 10 minutes covered, then fluff with chopsticks and serve with the family meal (mam com) of braises, stir-fries and canh soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nuoc Cham (Fish Sauce Dipping Sauce)

ingredients: 60 ml fish sauce (nuoc mam, e.g. Phu Quoc)
1–2 bird's eye chillies (ot hiem), finely chopped
steps: Stir the sugar into the warm water until fully dissolved.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice and taste; it should be balanced sweet, sour and salty, so adjust with more sugar or lime.
Stir in the garlic and chilli just before serving so they float on top.
Serve in small bowls with spring rolls, grilled meats, bun noodle bowls and broken rice; keeps 1 week refrigerated.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nuoc Mam Gung (Ginger Fish Sauce)

steps: Pound the ginger, garlic, chilli and sugar in a mortar and pestle to a coarse, juicy paste (or mince very finely).
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice and warm water until the sugar dissolves.
Taste and balance; it should be sharp with ginger, sweet and salty.
Serve with ga luoc (poached chicken), boiled duck or fried fish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Muoi Tieu Chanh (Salt, Pepper and Lime Dip)

ingredients: 1 tsp freshly cracked black pepper (Phu Quoc pepper if available)
steps: Put the salt and pepper side by side in a small saucer.
Squeeze the lime over just before eating and stir into a loose paste, adding chilli if you like.
Serve as a dip for poached chicken, boiled seafood, grilled squid or hot vit lon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tuong Ot (Vietnamese Chili Sauce)

ingredients: 250 g fresh red chillies (long red or a mix with bird's eye), stemmed
1 tsp tapioca starch mixed with 1 tbsp water
steps: Roughly chop the chillies and garlic and simmer them in the water over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Blend with the vinegar, sugar and salt until smooth.
Return to the pan and simmer 5 minutes, stirring, then add the starch slurry and cook 1 minute until glossy and lightly thickened.
Cool and store in a clean jar in the fridge for up to 3 weeks; serve with pho, banh mi and fried snacks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Do Chua (Pickled Carrot and Daikon)

ingredients: 300 g daikon radish (cu cai trang), peeled
steps: Cut the daikon and carrot into matchsticks about 5 cm long.
Toss with the salt and 1 tsp of the sugar and leave 15 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid and rinse briefly.
Dissolve the remaining sugar in the warm water and stir in the vinegar.
Pack the vegetables into a clean jar, pour over the brine to cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour (best overnight); serve with banh mi, bun and com tam.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dua Gia (Pickled Bean Sprouts)

ingredients: 400 g mung bean sprouts (gia), roots trimmed
4 Chinese chives (he), cut into 4 cm lengths
steps: Boil the water with the salt and sugar until dissolved, then cool to lukewarm and add the vinegar.
Rinse and drain the bean sprouts well and mix with the carrot and chives.
Pack into a clean jar, pour over the brine to cover and weigh down so everything is submerged.
Leave at room temperature overnight until tangy and slightly yellow, then refrigerate; eat within 4 days, traditionally alongside thit kho trung.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dua Cai Chua (Pickled Mustard Greens)

ingredients: 1 kg Asian mustard greens (cai be xanh)
steps: Wash the greens and leave them in the sun or air for 4–6 hours until wilted, then cut into 4 cm pieces.
Boil the water with the salt and sugar, then cool until just warm.
Pack the greens, shallots and chillies tightly into a clean jar and pour over the brine, weighing them down so they stay submerged.
Leave at room temperature 2–3 days until golden and pleasantly sour, then refrigerate; serve with braised pork or cook into canh chua soups.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Rau Muong Xao Toi (Water Spinach Stir-fried with Garlic)

ingredients: 500 g water spinach (rau muong; substitute spinach or pea shoots)
steps: Pick the water spinach into 8 cm lengths, discarding tough stem ends, wash and drain well.
Blanch in a large pot of boiling salted water for 30 seconds, then drain (this keeps it bright green).
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, fry half the garlic for 20 seconds until fragrant and golden.
Add the greens, soy sauce, sugar and salt and toss 1–2 minutes until just tender.
Top with the remaining garlic, lightly fried, and serve hot with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Rau Muong Luoc (Boiled Water Spinach)

ingredients: 500 g water spinach (rau muong), picked into 10 cm lengths
3 tbsp light soy sauce (or tuong) for dipping
steps: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a large pot.
Add the water spinach and boil 2 minutes until tender but still bright green, then lift out onto a plate.
Squeeze the lime into the cooking water to make a light, clear soup and taste for salt.
Serve the greens with soy sauce for dipping and the broth in bowls, as in a northern family meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dau Que Xao Toi (Garlic Green Beans)

ingredients: 400 g green beans, trimmed and cut into 5 cm lengths
1 tsp mushroom seasoning or 1/2 tsp sugar
steps: Blanch the beans in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beans, soy sauce, seasoning and water and stir-fry 3–4 minutes until tender-crisp and glossy.
Season with pepper and serve with steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bap Cai Luoc Cham Trung (Boiled Cabbage with Egg Fish Sauce Dip)

ingredients: 1/2 green cabbage (about 600 g), leaves separated and torn
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Boil the cabbage in the salted water for 4–5 minutes until tender but not limp, then drain, keeping the cooking water as a light soup.
Mash the eggs with a fork in a small bowl and stir in the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice and chilli.
Serve the cabbage with the egg fish sauce for dipping and the broth on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dau Phu Ran (Fried Tofu)

ingredients: 250 ml vegetable oil for shallow frying
steps: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 3 cm cubes or thick slabs, then sprinkle with salt.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat until shimmering (about 180°C).
Fry the tofu in batches 6–8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides; drain on paper.
Mix the soy sauce, spring onions and chilli and serve as a dip with the hot tofu and rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dau Phu Sot Ca Chua (Tofu in Tomato Sauce)

ingredients: 500 g firm tofu, cut into 3 cm cubes
steps: Shallow-fry the tofu in 2 tbsp oil over medium-high heat until golden on all sides, then set aside.
In the same pan, fry the shallots in the remaining oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and cook 6–8 minutes, mashing, until soft and saucy.
Season with soy sauce, sugar and salt, add 60 ml water and simmer 2 minutes.
Return the tofu and simmer 5 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until it is glossy and coats the tofu.
Scatter with spring onions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dau Phu Nhoi Thit Sot Ca Chua (Stuffed Tofu in Tomato Sauce)

ingredients: 4 blocks firm tofu (about 600 g), each cut into 2 triangles
5 g dried wood ear mushroom, soaked and chopped
steps: Mix the pork, wood ear, half the shallots, fish sauce and a pinch of pepper.
Cut a pocket into the long side of each tofu triangle and stuff with the pork mixture, pressing it level.
Pan-fry the tofu in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat, pork side down first, 8–10 minutes until golden all over.
Fry the remaining shallots in the remaining oil, add the tomatoes and sugar and cook 6 minutes until saucy, adding 100 ml water.
Add the tofu and simmer covered 8–10 minutes until the pork is cooked through; garnish with spring onions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Bi Do Nau Tom (Pumpkin and Shrimp Soup)

ingredients: 500 g pumpkin or kabocha squash (bi do), peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
200 g raw shrimp, peeled and roughly chopped
2 spring onions and a few sprigs rice paddy herb or coriander, chopped
steps: Season the shrimp with a little fish sauce and pepper.
Fry the shallots in the oil over medium heat for 1 minute, add the shrimp and stir 1 minute until pink.
Add the water, bring to a boil and add the pumpkin.
Simmer 12–15 minutes until the pumpkin is tender, skimming any foam, then season with fish sauce and salt.
Serve topped with spring onions and herbs alongside rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Muop (Luffa Soup)

ingredients: 2 angled or smooth luffa (muop, about 600 g; substitute zucchini), peeled and sliced
150 g raw shrimp, peeled and chopped (or dried shrimp, soaked)
steps: Fry the shallot in the oil over medium heat, add the shrimp and stir until pink.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil, skimming the foam.
Add the luffa and cook 3–4 minutes until just tender and translucent; do not overcook.
Season with fish sauce and salt, add spring onions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Kho Qua Nhoi Thit (Stuffed Bitter Melon Soup)

ingredients: 10 g glass noodles (mien), soaked and cut short
5 g dried wood ear mushroom, soaked and chopped
steps: Cut the bitter melons into 5 cm sections, scoop out the seeds and pith, and blanch 1 minute in salted boiling water to reduce bitterness.
Mix the pork, noodles, wood ear, shallots, 1/2 tbsp fish sauce and pepper, and stuff firmly into the melon rings.
Bring the water to a boil, add the stuffed melon and any leftover filling rolled into balls.
Simmer gently 30 minutes until the melon is tender and the pork cooked through, skimming foam, then season with the remaining fish sauce.
Serve garnished with herbs; traditionally eaten at Tet for luck.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Cai Thit Bam (Mustard Greens and Minced Pork Soup)

ingredients: 400 g Asian mustard greens (cai be xanh), cut into 4 cm pieces
steps: Season the pork with half the shallot, a dash of fish sauce and pepper.
Bring the water to a boil, add the remaining shallot and the pork in small pinches, stirring to separate, and skim the foam.
Simmer 5 minutes, then add the ginger and mustard greens.
Cook 3–4 minutes until the greens are tender, season with fish sauce and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Trung Ca Chua (Tomato Egg Drop Soup)

ingredients: 2 spring onions and a few sprigs coriander, chopped
steps: Fry the shallot in the oil over medium heat for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add the water, bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes; season with soy sauce and salt.
Stir the soup in a circle and slowly drizzle in the eggs, letting them set into ribbons for 30 seconds before stirring.
Add spring onions and coriander and serve hot with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Kho Trung (Caramelized Pork and Eggs)

ingredients: 1 kg pork belly or shoulder with skin, cut into 4 cm chunks
steps: Marinate the pork with the shallots, garlic, 2 tbsp fish sauce and pepper for 30 minutes; hard-boil and peel the eggs.
Melt the sugar with the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat until it turns a deep amber caramel, then add the pork and sear 5 minutes to coat.
Pour in the coconut water and enough water to just cover, bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Add the eggs and the remaining fish sauce and simmer gently, partially covered, 75–90 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce amber.
Serve with rice and dua gia or dua cai chua; this is a classic Tet dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Kho Tieu (Pepper Braised Pork)

ingredients: 600 g pork belly or shoulder, cut into 3 cm pieces
steps: Marinate the pork with half the shallots and garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce and half the pepper for 20 minutes.
Make a caramel with the sugar and oil in a clay pot or heavy pan over medium heat until dark amber.
Add the remaining shallots and garlic, then the pork, and sear 5 minutes until glazed.
Add the coconut water and remaining fish sauce, simmer covered 35–40 minutes, then uncover and reduce until the sauce is thick and sticky.
Finish with the rest of the pepper and spring onions; serve with rice and boiled vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ga Kho Gung (Ginger Braised Chicken)

ingredients: 800 g bone-in chicken thighs, chopped into pieces
steps: Marinate the chicken with half the shallots, 1 tbsp fish sauce and pepper for 20 minutes.
Make a caramel with the sugar and oil in a clay pot over medium heat until deep amber.
Add the remaining shallots and the ginger, fry 1 minute, then add the chicken and sear 5 minutes until coated.
Add the water and remaining fish sauce, cover and simmer 20–25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is sticky.
Serve with rice and boiled greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ga Xao Sa Ot (Lemongrass Chili Chicken)

ingredients: 600 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
steps: Marinate the chicken with half the lemongrass, the garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce, sugar and turmeric for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the remaining lemongrass, shallots and chillies 1–2 minutes until fragrant and golden.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 8–10 minutes until cooked through and lightly caramelized.
Season with the remaining fish sauce, toss until glossy and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ga Luoc (Poached Chicken)

ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken (ga ta, about 1.5 kg)
1 tsp ground turmeric mixed with 1 tsp oil (optional, for colour)
steps: Rub the chicken with salt, rinse, and put it in a pot with the ginger, shallots and cold water to cover.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, skim, then simmer very gently 30–35 minutes until the juices at the thigh run clear (75°C inside).
Turn off the heat and leave 10 minutes, then plunge the chicken into ice water to tighten the skin.
Brush with turmeric oil for a golden skin, chop into pieces and scatter with shredded lime leaves.
Serve with muoi tieu chanh or nuoc mam gung, using the broth for soup or chao.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Ga Chien Nuoc Mam (Fish Sauce Chicken Wings)

steps: Marinate the wings with 1 tbsp fish sauce, half the garlic and pepper for 20 minutes, then pat dry and toss in the starch.
Deep-fry at 170°C for 10–12 minutes in batches until golden and cooked through, then drain.
In a clean pan, fry the remaining garlic and chilli in 1 tbsp oil until fragrant, add the remaining fish sauce, sugar and water and bubble 1–2 minutes until syrupy.
Toss the wings in the sauce until glazed and serve with rice or as a beer snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Suon Xao Chua Ngot (Sweet and Sour Pork Ribs)

ingredients: 800 g pork spare ribs, cut into 4 cm pieces
steps: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and rinse, then marinate with 1 tbsp fish sauce and half the garlic for 15 minutes.
Fry the ribs in the oil over medium-high heat 8–10 minutes until golden on all sides.
Add the shallots and remaining garlic, then the sugar, vinegar, ketchup, remaining fish sauce and 150 ml water.
Simmer covered 15 minutes, then uncover and reduce, turning the ribs, until the sauce is sticky and the ribs tender.
Scatter with spring onions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Ba Chi Luoc (Boiled Pork Belly)

ingredients: 600 g skin-on pork belly in one piece
4 tbsp mam tom (fermented shrimp paste) or nuoc cham for dipping
1 bunch fresh herbs (perilla, Vietnamese mint, lettuce)
steps: Scrub the pork skin, rinse and put in a pot with the shallots, ginger, salt and cold water to cover.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently 25–30 minutes until a skewer goes through without pink juices.
Plunge into cold water for 5 minutes so the meat firms up, then slice thinly across the grain.
Beat the mam tom with lime juice, a little sugar and chilli until foamy (or use nuoc cham).
Serve the pork with herbs, rice or rice vermicelli and the dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Ba Roi Chien Nuoc Mam (Fish Sauce Fried Pork Belly)

ingredients: 600 g pork belly, sliced 1 cm thick
steps: Season the pork with 1 tbsp fish sauce and pepper for 10 minutes.
Fry the pork in the oil in a pan over medium heat 10–12 minutes, turning, until golden and the fat has rendered; pour off excess fat.
Add the garlic and chilli and fry 30 seconds, then add the remaining fish sauce, sugar and 1 tbsp water.
Toss over medium heat 2–3 minutes until the sauce caramelizes and clings to the pork; serve with rice and boiled vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Nuong Sa (Grilled Lemongrass Pork)

ingredients: 600 g pork shoulder or collar, sliced 5 mm thick
steps: Mix the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, oil, pepper and dark soy, add the pork and marinate at least 1 hour (or overnight in the fridge).
Heat a charcoal grill or grill pan to high.
Grill the pork 3–4 minutes per side until cooked through with charred, caramelized edges.
Serve with broken rice (com tam), rice vermicelli (bun), herbs, do chua and nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Heo Quay (Vietnamese Crispy Roast Pork)

ingredients: 1.2 kg skin-on pork belly in one slab
1 tbsp coarse salt for the skin
steps: Boil the pork 10 minutes, drain, and prick the skin all over with a skewer or fork.
Rub the meat side (not the skin) with five-spice, sugar, fish sauce and garlic; brush the skin with vinegar and rub with salt.
Refrigerate uncovered, skin up, overnight to dry the skin.

Wrap the meat sides in foil, leaving skin exposed, and roast at 180°C for 45 minutes, then raise to 230°C for 20–30 minutes until the skin puffs and crackles; the meat should reach at least 71°C inside.
Rest 15 minutes, chop into pieces and serve with rice, banh mi or rice vermicelli and nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tom Rim (Caramelized Shrimp)

ingredients: 500 g medium shrimp, shell on, legs and feelers trimmed
steps: Season the shrimp with 1 tsp fish sauce and pepper for 10 minutes.
Fry the shallots and garlic in the oil over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and sear 2 minutes until they turn pink, then add the sugar and remaining fish sauce.
Cook over medium heat 5–7 minutes, tossing, until the sauce reduces to a sticky, dark glaze and the shrimp are cooked through.
Add spring onions and pepper and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Sot Ca Chua (Fried Fish in Tomato Sauce)

ingredients: 800 g whole fish or thick steaks (tilapia, mackerel or snakehead), cleaned
2 spring onions and a few sprigs dill, chopped
steps: Pat the fish dry, season with salt and fry in 3 tbsp oil over medium-high heat 5–6 minutes per side until golden; set aside.
Fry the shallots and garlic in the remaining oil, add the tomatoes and cook 6–8 minutes until saucy.
Season with fish sauce and sugar and add 100 ml water.
Return the fish and simmer 5 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until the flesh flakes easily.
Top with spring onions and dill and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Muc Nhoi Thit (Pork-stuffed Squid)

ingredients: 8 medium squid tubes (about 600 g), cleaned, tentacles reserved
10 g glass noodles, soaked and cut short
5 g dried wood ear mushroom, soaked and chopped
steps: Chop the tentacles and mix with the pork, noodles, wood ear, half the shallots, 1 tbsp fish sauce and pepper.
Stuff the squid tubes three-quarters full and close with a toothpick.
Pan-fry in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden and the filling is firm (cooked through).
Fry the remaining shallots in the remaining oil, add the tomatoes and remaining fish sauce and cook to a sauce, then simmer the squid in it 5 minutes.
Slice into rings and serve with rice or nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Trung Chien Hanh (Vietnamese Scallion Omelette)

steps: Beat the eggs with the fish sauce, pepper and spring onions until well mixed.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Pour in the eggs and cook 2 minutes until the base is golden, then flip and cook 1 minute more until set.
Cut into wedges and serve with rice and nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cha Trung (Steamed Egg and Pork Meatloaf)

ingredients: 20 g glass noodles, soaked and cut short
5 g dried wood ear mushroom, soaked and chopped
steps: Separate 2 egg yolks and set aside; mix the pork, remaining whole eggs and whites, noodles, wood ear, shallots, fish sauce, sugar and pepper.
Press into an oiled heatproof dish about 4 cm deep.
Steam over medium-high heat 25–30 minutes until firm and the centre is cooked through.
Brush the top with the beaten yolks and steam 3–5 minutes more until set and golden.
Cut into wedges and serve with com tam or rice and nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Gio Lua (Cha Lua, Vietnamese Pork Sausage)

ingredients: 500 g very lean pork loin or leg, well chilled
2 banana leaves (substitute foil lined with baking paper)
steps: Cut the pork into cubes, toss with fish sauce and sugar and freeze 30 minutes until very cold.
Process the pork with the ice, baking powder, starch and oil in a food processor 5–6 minutes until a smooth, sticky, pale paste forms.
Wrap tightly into a 6 cm thick log in softened banana leaves, then foil, and tie firmly with string.
Simmer in water (or steam) 50–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the centre is cooked through.
Cool, slice and serve with banh mi, banh cuon, sticky rice or at Tet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Goi Ga Bap Cai (Chicken and Cabbage Salad)

ingredients: 2 bone-in chicken thighs or 1 breast (about 400 g)
1 bunch Vietnamese coriander (rau ram) or mint, chopped
steps: Poach the chicken in simmering salted water 20–25 minutes until cooked through, cool and shred.
Soak the onion in cold water with a little vinegar for 10 minutes to soften its bite, then drain.
Whisk the fish sauce, sugar and lime juice with 2 tbsp water and a chopped chilli.
Toss the cabbage, carrot, onion, chicken and herbs with the dressing, top with peanuts and serve with rice porridge or as a starter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Goi Ngo Sen (Lotus Stem Salad)

ingredients: 300 g pickled lotus rootlets (ngo sen, sold in jars; or fresh), halved lengthwise
150 g boiled pork belly, thinly sliced
2 tbsp roasted peanuts and fried shallots
steps: Rinse the lotus stems, squeeze dry and toss with the carrot.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, 1 chopped garlic clove and chilli into a dressing.
Toss the lotus, carrot, shrimp, pork and herbs with the dressing.
Top with peanuts and fried shallots and serve with prawn crackers (banh phong tom).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Goi Bap Chuoi (Banana Blossom Salad)

ingredients: 1 banana blossom (bap chuoi), outer bracts removed
1 lime, juiced, plus water for soaking
200 g cooked chicken or boiled pork, shredded
1 small bunch Vietnamese coriander (rau ram) and mint, chopped
steps: Thinly slice the banana blossom crosswise and drop straight into water with lime juice to stop browning; soak 15 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Whisk the fish sauce, sugar and lime juice with a chopped chilli and garlic clove.
Toss the banana blossom with the meat, herbs and dressing.
Top with peanuts and fried shallots and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chao Ga (Chicken Rice Porridge)

ingredients: 1 small chicken or 800 g bone-in thighs
150 g jasmine rice (plus 2 tbsp sticky rice for creaminess)
30 g ginger, sliced, plus 1 tbsp julienned for topping
Fried shallots, black pepper and lime to serve
steps: Poach the chicken with the sliced ginger and shallots in the water 30–35 minutes until cooked through; remove and shred, keeping the broth.
Dry-toast the rinsed rice in a pan 3–4 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant.
Simmer the rice in the broth, stirring often, 30–40 minutes until broken down and creamy.
Season with fish sauce and serve topped with chicken, spring onions, julienned ginger, fried shallots and pepper, with nuoc mam gung on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chao Long (Pork Offal Congee)

ingredients: 500 g mixed pork offal (intestines, heart, liver, tongue), thoroughly cleaned
1 piece cooked pork blood cake (huyet), cubed
3 spring onions and 1 bunch rice paddy herb, chopped
Fried shallots, pepper, lime and chilli to serve
steps: Rub the intestines with salt and vinegar, rinse well, and blanch all the offal and bones in boiling water 3 minutes, then rinse.
Simmer the bones and offal (except liver) in the water 50–60 minutes until tender, adding the liver for the last 10 minutes so it is fully cooked; lift out and slice.
Toast the rice and simmer it in the broth 30–40 minutes until creamy, adding the blood cake for the last 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and serve topped with sliced offal, herbs, fried shallots and pepper, with quay (fried dough) on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chao Vit (Duck Congee)

ingredients: Nuoc mam gung, Vietnamese mint and fried shallots to serve
steps: Rub the duck with salt and ginger, rinse, then simmer with the sliced ginger and shallots in the water 50–60 minutes until tender and cooked through.
Lift out the duck, cool and chop into pieces.
Toast the rice and simmer it in the duck broth 30–40 minutes until creamy, seasoning with fish sauce.
Serve the congee with spring onions and fried shallots and the duck on a plate alongside, dipped in nuoc mam gung, with goi (cabbage salad).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Rieu Cua (Crab and Tomato Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 300 g minced crab meat or jarred crab paste in soya oil (gia vi nau bun rieu)
1 tbsp tamarind or rice vinegar for sourness
Fried tofu, bean sprouts, perilla and shredded banana blossom to serve
steps: Mix the crab, pork, eggs, half the shallots and 1 tbsp fish sauce into a loose batter.
Fry the remaining shallots and tomatoes in a little oil 3 minutes, then add the stock and bring to a boil.
Lower to a gentle simmer and spoon in the crab mixture; it will float up as soft rafts (rieu) after 8–10 minutes when cooked through.
Add the fried tofu, season with fish sauce and tamarind and simmer 5 minutes.
Ladle over noodles and serve with herbs, sprouts, lime and mam tom on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mien Ga (Chicken Glass Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 200 g glass noodles (mien dong, mung bean or cassava)
5 g dried wood ear or shiitake, soaked and sliced
Spring onions, Vietnamese coriander and fried shallots to serve
steps: Simmer the chicken with ginger and shallots in the water 35 minutes until cooked through; remove, shred and strain the broth.
Season the broth with fish sauce and sugar and add the mushrooms; simmer 5 minutes.
Soak the glass noodles in warm water 10 minutes, then dip them in the boiling broth 1 minute until glassy.
Divide the noodles into bowls, top with chicken and herbs and ladle over the hot broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mien Xao Cua (Stir-fried Glass Noodles with Crab)

ingredients: 200 g glass noodles (mien), soaked 10 minutes and drained
5 g dried wood ear, soaked and sliced
3 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
steps: Fry the garlic in the oil in a wok over high heat until fragrant, add the wood ear and stir 1 minute.
Push aside, scramble the eggs until just set, then add the noodles with 60 ml water, fish sauce and oyster sauce.
Toss 3–4 minutes until the noodles absorb the sauce and turn soft and glossy.
Fold in the crab, bean sprouts and spring onions and toss 1 minute until hot; serve with pepper and coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mi Xao Gion (Crispy Fried Noodles)

ingredients: 200 g pork or beef, thinly sliced
300 g mixed vegetables (choy sum, carrot, baby corn, mushrooms)
1 tbsp tapioca starch mixed with 3 tbsp water
steps: Blanch the noodles 30 seconds, drain well, and fry in 5 mm hot oil as flat nests 4–5 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Stir-fry the garlic, meat and shrimp in 2 tbsp oil over high heat 3 minutes until cooked through.
Add the vegetables and stir-fry 2 minutes, then the stock, oyster sauce and fish sauce.
Thicken with the starch slurry until glossy and pour over the crispy noodles; serve at once with soy sauce and pickled chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Com Chien Duong Chau (Yangzhou Fried Rice)

ingredients: 1.5 tbsp fish sauce or soy sauce
steps: Fry the lap xuong in a dry wok over medium heat 3 minutes until the fat runs; add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes until pink, then remove.
Add the oil and garlic, then the eggs, and scramble briefly.
Add the rice and stir-fry over high heat 5 minutes, pressing out lumps, until hot and slightly toasty.
Return the sausage and shrimp with the peas and carrot, season with fish sauce and toss 2 minutes; finish with spring onions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Bao (Vietnamese Steamed Buns)

ingredients: 500 g banh bao flour or low-protein flour
2 lap xuong (Chinese sausage), sliced, and 4 quail eggs, boiled
5 g wood ear, soaked and chopped
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, milk and oil into a soft, smooth dough; knead 10 minutes and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the pork, wood ear, fish sauce and pepper for the filling.
Divide the dough into 8, roll each into a 12 cm round, fill with pork, a slice of sausage and half a quail egg, and pleat closed on a square of baking paper.
Rest 20 minutes, then steam over boiling water 18–20 minutes until puffed and the filling is cooked through; don't lift the lid early.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Mi Op La (Fried Egg Banh Mi)

ingredients: 1 tbsp Maggi seasoning or light soy sauce
Cucumber slices, coriander and chilli to serve
steps: Warm the baguettes in the oven at 180°C for 3 minutes until crisp.
Heat the butter in a small pan (or two individual cast-iron pans) over medium heat and crack in the eggs.
Fry 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and edges crispy, yolks runny.
Drizzle with Maggi and pepper and serve straight in the pan with the baguette for dipping and cucumber, coriander and chilli on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Xoi Gac (Gac Fruit Sticky Rice)

ingredients: 150 g gac fruit pulp (frozen gac aril; substitute 1 tbsp gac powder)
steps: Soak the glutinous rice in water overnight, then drain well.
Mix the gac pulp with the rice wine, rubbing the red flesh off the seeds, then massage it into the rice with the salt until evenly red; discard the seeds.
Steam the rice in a cloth-lined steamer over boiling water 25 minutes, stirring once.
Stir in the sugar, oil and coconut cream and steam 10 minutes more until glossy and tender.
Press into moulds and serve at Tet, weddings and ancestor offerings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Xoi Dau Phong (Peanut Sticky Rice)

ingredients: 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds mixed with 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp sugar (muoi me)
steps: Soak the rice and peanuts separately in water overnight; drain.
Boil the peanuts 15 minutes until half-cooked, then drain and mix with the rice and salt.
Steam in a cloth-lined steamer over boiling water 30–35 minutes, stirring halfway, until the rice is tender and the peanuts soft.
Drizzle with coconut cream, steam 2 minutes more and serve topped with sesame salt.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau Thai (Vietnamese Thai-style Hot Pot)

ingredients: 3 stalks lemongrass, bruised, and 5 lime leaves
4 tomatoes and 200 g pineapple, cut into chunks
2 tbsp fish sauce and 2 tbsp lime juice
400 g shrimp, peeled, and 300 g squid, scored
300 g beef or fish fillet, thinly sliced
500 g greens (water spinach, napa cabbage, morning glory)
500 g fresh rice noodles or instant noodles
steps: Fry the tomatoes in a little oil 3 minutes, add the stock, lemongrass, lime leaves, pineapple and tom yum paste and simmer 15 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice and a little sugar to a hot-sour balance, then transfer to a tabletop hot pot.
Keep the broth at a steady boil and let diners cook the seafood 2–3 minutes and beef 1 minute until just done, then mushrooms and greens.
Add noodles to the broth at the end and serve with chilli-salt dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau De (Goat Hot Pot)

ingredients: 1.5 kg bone-in goat meat, cut into chunks
2 tbsp fermented tofu (chao) mashed with 1 tbsp sugar, for dipping
30 g lotus seeds, 4 red dates and 2 pieces dried thuoc bac (Chinese herbal mix)
500 g greens (water spinach, Chinese mugwort/ngai cuu), and 400 g rice noodles
steps: Blanch the goat in boiling water with ginger 5 minutes to remove odour; rinse.
Brown the goat in a little oil with the lemongrass and remaining ginger 5 minutes.
Add the water, herbs, lotus seeds and red dates and simmer gently 1.5 hours until tender, adding taro for the last 20 minutes; season with fish sauce.
Serve at the table on a burner with greens to cook in the broth, noodles, and fermented tofu dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Hot Vit Lon (Balut)

ingredients: 4 fertilized duck eggs (hot vit lon), 17–19 days, bought fresh from a trusted Asian market
1 tbsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper with 1 lime (muoi tieu chanh)
steps: Put the eggs in a pot of cold water and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Simmer 20–25 minutes so the egg is fully cooked through.
Serve hot in egg cups: crack the wider end, sip the broth, season with salt-pepper-lime and eat with rau ram and ginger.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Phong Tom (Shrimp Chips)

ingredients: 250 g raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Blend the shrimp, garlic, salt, sugar and pepper to a smooth paste, then knead in the tapioca starch to a firm dough.
Shape into 4 cm thick logs, wrap and steam 45–60 minutes until fully cooked and translucent.
Cool, then refrigerate overnight until firm; slice as thinly as possible (1–2 mm).
Dry the slices in the sun or a 60°C oven for several hours until hard and brittle.
Fry a few at a time in 180°C oil for a few seconds until they puff, then drain; store the dried chips airtight.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Trung Thu (Vietnamese Mooncakes)

ingredients: 140 g golden syrup (nuoc duong banh nuong)
1/2 tsp lye water (nuoc tro) or 1/4 tsp baking soda in 1 tsp water
400 g sweet lotus seed or mung bean paste
1 egg yolk beaten with 1 tbsp water, for glaze
steps: Mix the golden syrup, oil and lye water, stir in the flour into a soft dough, cover and rest for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Steam the salted yolks 8 minutes, then wrap each in 50 g lotus or mung bean paste.
Wrap each filling ball in about 25 g dough, press into a floured mooncake mould and unmould onto a lined tray.
Bake at 180°C for 8 minutes, cool 10 minutes, brush thinly with egg glaze and bake 10–12 minutes more until deep golden.
Store airtight 1–2 days before eating so the crust softens; serve with tea at the Mid-Autumn Festival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Deo (Snowskin Mooncake)

ingredients: 200 g cooked glutinous rice flour (bot nep rang)
1 tsp grapefruit-flower essence (nuoc hoa buoi) or vanilla
400 g sweet mung bean paste mixed with 50 g candied winter melon (mut bi), chopped
steps: Boil the sugar and water 5 minutes into a light syrup, cool, and stir in the flower essence.
Gradually knead the syrup and oil into the cooked rice flour to a soft, smooth, slightly sticky dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll the filling into 50 g balls and wrap each in 30 g dough.
Press into a mould dusted with rice flour, unmould and leave a few hours to set; serve at room temperature with tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mut Dua (Candied Coconut Ribbons)

ingredients: 500 g young-mature coconut flesh, peeled into long thin ribbons
Natural colours: 1 tbsp pandan juice, gac or butterfly pea flower water (optional)
steps: Soak the coconut ribbons in water with lime juice 10 minutes, then drain.
Divide into batches and toss with colour if using, then mix with the sugar and leave 1 hour until the sugar dissolves into syrup.
Cook over low heat 40–50 minutes, stirring gently, until the syrup evaporates and sugar crystallizes on the ribbons.
Spread on a tray to cool and dry; store airtight and serve on the Tet candy tray (khay mut).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mut Gung (Candied Ginger)

steps: Slice the ginger thinly, soak in water with salt and lime juice for 2 hours, then boil 5 minutes and drain to reduce the heat.
Mix the ginger with the sugar and leave overnight until a syrup forms.
Cook over low heat, stirring, 40–50 minutes until the syrup evaporates and white sugar crystals coat the slices.
Cool on a tray and store airtight; serve at Tet with hot tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Dau Xanh (Mung Bean Sweet Soup)

ingredients: 2 tbsp tapioca starch mixed with 3 tbsp water
200 ml coconut milk with a pinch of salt
steps: Soak the mung beans 2 hours, then rinse and drain.
Simmer the beans with the water and pandan 25–30 minutes until soft and creamy.
Stir in the sugar, then the tapioca slurry, and cook 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Warm the coconut milk with the salt; serve the che warm or with ice, topped with coconut milk and toasted sesame.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Dau Den (Black Bean Sweet Soup)

ingredients: 200 g black beans (dau den xanh long)
steps: Soak the beans overnight, then drain.
Simmer with the water and pandan 45–60 minutes until the beans are tender but intact.
Stir in the sugar and salt and simmer 10 minutes so the beans absorb the sweetness.
Serve chilled over crushed ice, with coconut milk if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Flan (Vietnamese Caramel Flan)

ingredients: 100 g sugar (for caramel) plus 2 tbsp water
3 tbsp strong black coffee and crushed ice to serve
steps: Cook the sugar and water over medium heat until deep amber caramel, then pour into 6 ramekins.
Warm the milk and condensed milk, then whisk gently into the eggs and yolks with the vanilla; strain twice to remove bubbles.
Pour over the caramel, cover each with foil and steam over gentle heat 25–30 minutes (or bake in a water bath at 150°C) until just set with a slight wobble.
Chill at least 3 hours, then turn out and serve with crushed ice and a drizzle of black coffee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sua Chua (Vietnamese Yogurt)

steps: Mix the condensed milk with the hot water, then stir in the milk; it should feel warm, about 40–45°C.
Whisk the yogurt starter in a separate bowl until smooth, then stir it into the milk mixture.
Pour into small jars, cover and keep warm at about 40°C (in a cooler with warm water or an oven with the light on) for 8 hours until set.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours and serve cold, plain or with coffee or fruit.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tau Hu Nuoc Duong (Tofu Pudding in Ginger Syrup)

ingredients: 1 tsp gypsum (calcium sulfate) or 2 tsp glucono delta-lactone (GDL) dissolved in 60 ml water
steps: Soak the soybeans overnight, blend with the water and strain through cloth to make soy milk.
Bring the soy milk to a boil, stirring constantly, and simmer 10 minutes; cool to about 85°C.
Put the coagulant in a pot, pour the hot soy milk in from a height, cover and leave undisturbed 20 minutes until set into a soft curd.
Simmer the sugar, ginger and water 10 minutes into a syrup and serve spoonfuls of warm tofu pudding with the ginger syrup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Phe Sua Da (Iced Coffee with Condensed Milk)

ingredients: 25 g dark-roast Vietnamese ground coffee (robusta, e.g. Trung Nguyen)
steps: Put the condensed milk in a glass and set a phin filter on top with the coffee.
Pour in 20 ml hot water to bloom for 30 seconds, then fill the phin and cover.
Let it drip slowly for 4–5 minutes until finished.
Stir the coffee into the condensed milk and pour over a glass full of ice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Phe Den Da (Iced Black Coffee)

steps: Set a phin filter over a cup with the coffee, bloom with 20 ml hot water for 30 seconds, then fill and cover.
Drip for 4–5 minutes.
Stir in sugar if using and pour over a tall glass of ice; serve with a glass of tra da.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tra Da (Iced Green Tea)

ingredients: 10 g Vietnamese green tea leaves (che Thai Nguyen) or jasmine tea
steps: Rinse the tea leaves quickly with a splash of boiling water and discard it.
Steep the leaves in 1.5 litres of water at about 85°C for 5–8 minutes, then strain.
Cool and pour over glasses full of ice; serve free with street food and coffee, unsweetened.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nuoc Mia (Sugarcane Juice)

ingredients: 1 kg fresh sugarcane stalks, peeled (or 500 ml bottled pure cane juice)
1 small piece pandan or a slice of ginger (optional)
steps: Cut the peeled sugarcane into short lengths.
Press through a sugarcane press or a heavy-duty juicer, adding the kumquat and pandan as you press.
Strain and serve immediately over ice before the juice oxidizes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sinh To Bo (Avocado Smoothie)

steps: Scoop the avocado flesh into a blender.
Add the condensed milk, milk and ice.
Blend until thick and silky, then taste and add more condensed milk if needed; serve immediately with a spoon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nuoc Rau Ma (Pennywort Juice)

ingredients: 200 g fresh pennywort (rau ma, Centella asiatica), washed
2 tbsp coconut milk or mung bean paste (optional)
steps: Soak the pennywort in salted water 10 minutes, rinse and chop roughly.
Blend with the water until very fine, then strain through a fine sieve or cloth.
Sweeten with sugar and serve over ice, topped with coconut milk or mung bean if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chanh Muoi (Salted Lime Drink)

ingredients: 2 salted preserved limes (chanh muoi, from a jar; substitute preserved lemons)
250 ml cold water or soda water
steps: Put the salted limes in a glass with the jar syrup and sugar and crush them with a spoon.
Add ice and pour over the water or soda.
Stir well and taste for a sweet-salty-sour balance; serve as a cooling summer drink.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sua Dau Nanh (Vietnamese Soy Milk)

steps: Soak the soybeans overnight, rub off the skins and rinse.
Blend with the water until smooth and strain through a cloth, squeezing well.
Bring to a boil with the pandan, stirring constantly, and simmer 15–20 minutes, skimming foam, until no raw bean taste remains.
Stir in sugar and salt and serve hot or chilled over ice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nuoc Sam (Herbal Cooling Drink)

ingredients: 1 packet dried nuoc sam mix (rau ma, mia lau, la dua, rau bap) from an Asian grocer
2 stalks sugarcane, peeled and cut (or 100 g rock sugar)
steps: Rinse the dried herbs and put them in a pot with the water, sugarcane and longan.
Bring to a boil and simmer gently 30–40 minutes until the liquid turns amber and fragrant.
Strain, stir in the rock sugar to taste and cool.
Serve chilled over ice as a cooling drink on hot days.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pho Bo Ha Noi (Hanoi Beef Pho)

ingredients: 2 kg beef marrow and knuckle bones
300 g beef sirloin or eye of round, sliced paper-thin
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 black cardamom (thao qua), 3 cloves
3 tbsp fish sauce (nuoc mam), plus 1 tbsp rock sugar
1 kg fresh flat rice noodles (banh pho), or 500 g dried
4 spring onions, sliced; 1 bunch cilantro; 1 white onion, thinly sliced
To serve: lime wedges, sliced bird's eye chilli, chilli vinegar (tuong ot dam toi)
steps: Blanch the bones in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse well to get a clear broth.

Cover the bones and brisket with 5 litres fresh water, add the charred onion and ginger and the dry-toasted spices, and simmer very gently for 6 hours, skimming often; lift the brisket out once tender after about 2 hours and slice it.
Season the strained broth with fish sauce, rock sugar and salt; Hanoi pho should taste clean and savoury rather than sweet.
Scald the noodles in boiling water for 10 seconds, divide into bowls and top with brisket, raw sirloin slices, spring onion and onion.
Ladle the boiling broth over so the raw beef cooks pink, and serve with lime, chilli and chilli-garlic vinegar; Hanoians skip the herb plate and hoisin of the south.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pho Ga (Chicken Pho)

ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken (ga ta), about 1.6 kg
2 star anise, 1 tsp coriander seeds, 1 small cinnamon stick
3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, salt
1 kg fresh flat rice noodles (banh pho)
4 spring onions and a handful of Vietnamese coriander (rau ram), chopped
steps: Rub the chicken with salt and ginger, rinse, and blanch the bones for 3 minutes, then rinse.

Simmer the chicken and bones in 4 litres water with charred onion, ginger and toasted spices; remove the whole chicken after 40 minutes when the juices at the thigh run clear, plunge into iced water, and keep the bones simmering another hour.
Strain the broth and season with fish sauce, sugar and salt.
Shred or chop the chicken with its skin and scald the noodles in boiling water for 10 seconds.
Arrange noodles, chicken, spring onion, rau ram and shredded lime leaf in bowls, pour over boiling broth and serve with lime and chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pho Cuon (Rolled Pho)

ingredients: 500 g uncut fresh rice noodle sheets (banh pho la)
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp oil
1 head lettuce and a bunch each of mint, cilantro and perilla
Dipping sauce: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp sugar, 150 ml warm water, garlic and chilli
1 small green papaya or carrot, thinly sliced and lightly pickled
steps: Marinate the beef with half the garlic, fish sauce and oyster sauce for 10 minutes.
Fry the remaining garlic in oil over high heat until fragrant, add the beef and stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes until just cooked.
Cut the rice sheets into 15 x 20 cm rectangles, lay lettuce and herbs on each, add some beef and roll up tightly like a spring roll.
Mix the dipping sauce until the sugar dissolves, add the pickled papaya and serve the rolls with it, Ngu Xa island style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pho Xao (Stir-fried Pho Noodles)

ingredients: 400 g fresh flat rice noodles (banh pho)
150 g Chinese kale or choy sum (cai ngot), cut in lengths
1 onion, sliced; 2 spring onions, cut in lengths
2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp oyster sauce
steps: Separate the noodle sheets by hand and toss with 1 tsp soy sauce so they do not stick.
Stir-fry the beef with half the garlic in 1 tbsp oil over very high heat for 1 minute and set aside.
Fry the remaining garlic and onion, add the greens and cook 2 minutes until bright green.
Add the noodles and sauces and toss over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until lightly charred at the edges.
Return the beef with spring onion, toss, sprinkle with pepper and serve with chilli and a small bowl of vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pho Chien Phong (Puffed Fried Pho)

ingredients: 500 g uncut fresh rice noodle sheets, cut into 6 cm squares
200 g Chinese kale or bok choy, 1 carrot, sliced
1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar
1 tbsp tapioca starch mixed with 150 ml water
steps: Stack 2 to 3 sheets per square and deep-fry at 180 C, pressing gently, until they puff into golden pillows, about 2 minutes; drain.
Stir-fry the beef with garlic over high heat for 1 minute and remove.
Stir-fry the vegetables for 2 minutes, add the sauces and 150 ml water, then thicken with the starch slurry until glossy.
Return the beef, then spoon the gravy over the puffed noodles and serve at once so they stay crisp at the edges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pho Tron (Dry Mixed Pho)

ingredients: 200 g roast or boiled beef or chicken, sliced
2 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp water
2 tbsp roasted peanuts, crushed; 2 tbsp fried shallots
Handful of lettuce, Thai basil, mint and rau ram
1 small cucumber and some pickled papaya-carrot
steps: Mix fish sauce, lime, sugar, water, garlic and chilli into a sweet-sour dressing.
Scald the noodles in boiling water for 10 seconds and drain well.
Put herbs and cucumber in the bowl, add noodles and meat, and pour over the dressing.
Top with peanuts, fried shallots and pickles, toss well and serve with a small cup of hot broth on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Cha (Hanoi Grilled Pork with Rice Noodles)

ingredients: 400 g pork shoulder, minced, formed into small patties
3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp caramel (nuoc mau) or 1 tbsp sugar, 4 shallots minced, black pepper
Dipping broth: 5 tbsp fish sauce, 5 tbsp sugar, 4 tbsp rice vinegar, 600 ml warm water
Lettuce, perilla (tia to), Vietnamese balm (kinh gioi), mint
steps: Marinate both porks with fish sauce, caramel, shallots and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Mix the dipping broth ingredients until dissolved, add kohlrabi and carrot slices and leave 15 minutes.
Grill the patties and belly in a hinged basket over charcoal, turning, for 8 to 10 minutes until caramelised and cooked through.
Drop the hot pork into bowls of the warm broth, add garlic and chilli, and serve with bun and herbs to dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cha Ca La Vong (Hanoi Turmeric Fish with Dill)

ingredients: 700 g firm white fish such as hemibagrus (ca lang) or monkfish, in 4 cm pieces
1 tbsp fresh turmeric and 1 tbsp galangal, pounded
2 tbsp fermented rice (me) or 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp shrimp paste (mam tom), 1 tbsp fish sauce
2 large bunches dill (thi la) and 6 spring onions, cut in lengths
Mam tom with lime, sugar and chilli, or nuoc cham, to serve
steps: Marinate the fish with turmeric, galangal, fermented rice, shrimp paste and fish sauce for 2 hours.
Grill the fish over charcoal or under a hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and almost cooked.
At the table, heat the oil in a pan on a burner, add the fish and fry 2 minutes, then pile on dill and spring onion and turn for 30 seconds until just wilted.
Spoon into bowls of bun, top with peanuts and dress with whipped mam tom or nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Cuon (Steamed Rice Rolls)

ingredients: 300 g rice flour, 30 g tapioca starch, 750 ml water, 1/2 tsp salt
30 g dried wood ear mushrooms (moc nhi), soaked and chopped
3 shallots, minced, 1 tbsp fish sauce, pepper
200 g Vietnamese pork roll (cha lua), sliced
Nuoc cham with a few drops of ca cuong essence (optional)
steps: Whisk the flours, salt and water and rest 4 hours for a silky batter.
Fry shallots, add pork and mushrooms, season and cook 6 minutes until dry and crumbly.
Stretch a cloth over a pot of boiling water, spread a thin ladle of batter on it, cover and steam 30 to 45 seconds until translucent.
Lift the sheet with a bamboo stick, add a spoon of filling and fold into a roll; repeat.
Serve warm topped with fried shallots, with cha lua, herbs and warm nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Thang (Hanoi Chicken, Egg and Pork Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 1 chicken (1.5 kg) and 500 g pork bones
10 g dried shrimp and 3 dried shiitake, soaked
3 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
200 g Vietnamese pork roll (gio lua), finely shredded
1/2 tsp shrimp paste (mam tom) and a few drops ca cuong essence (optional)
steps: Simmer the chicken, bones, dried shrimp and mushrooms in 4 litres water; remove the chicken after 40 minutes when cooked through and keep the broth simmering 1 more hour.
Fry the egg in a very thin layer in an oiled pan over low heat, roll and slice into hair-thin strands.
Shred the chicken and mushrooms finely; season the strained broth with fish sauce and sugar until clear and delicate.
Fill bowls with bun and arrange chicken, egg, gio lua and mushroom in neat sections, add herbs and pour over boiling broth.
Serve with a dab of mam tom and chilli on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Dau Mam Tom (Rice Noodles, Fried Tofu and Shrimp Paste)

ingredients: 800 g fresh tofu (dau Mo), cut in squares
500 g pork leg, boiled and thinly sliced
300 g compressed rice vermicelli (bun la), cut into squares
200 g green rice pork patties (cha com), fried
1 lime, 1 tsp sugar, 1 chilli, 1 tbsp hot oil
steps: Simmer the pork leg in salted water for 35 minutes until a skewer meets no pink juices, plunge in cold water and slice thinly.
Fry the drained tofu in hot oil for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp and golden.
Whisk the mam tom with lime juice, sugar and a spoon of hot oil until it froths and lightens, then add chilli.
Arrange everything on a bamboo tray lined with banana leaf and serve with herbs and the frothy dip; if mam tom is too strong, use nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Oc (Snail Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 1.5 kg river or apple snails (oc nhoi), purged in rice water for 2 hours
3 tbsp fermented rice vinegar (giam bong) or tamarind water
5 shallots, sliced, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp turmeric
Fish sauce, sugar, spring onions, perilla, shredded banana blossom
steps: Simmer the bones for 1 hour; boil the snails 5 minutes, pick out the meat, trim, and rinse with salt and vinegar.
Fry the shallots, then the tomatoes with turmeric until saucy, and add to the strained broth with the giam bong.
Quickly fry the snail meat with a little shallot for 2 minutes and add the tofu to the broth.
Season sour-savoury with fish sauce and sugar, simmer 5 minutes, and ladle over bun with snails and herbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Ca Ha Noi (Hanoi Fried Fish Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 600 g snakehead or tilapia fillet, cut into strips
1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp galangal paste, 1 tbsp fish sauce
3 tomatoes, quartered; 2 tbsp giam bong or tamarind
Water spinach stems (rau muong) and banana blossom, shredded
steps: Marinate the fish with turmeric, galangal and fish sauce for 20 minutes.
Deep-fry at 180 C for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp and golden right through.
Fry the shallots and tomatoes, add the stock and giam bong, and simmer 15 minutes; season with fish sauce.
Put bun in bowls, add fish, dill and spring onion, pour over the hot sour broth and serve with the raw greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Moc (Pork Meatball Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 300 g pork paste (gio song) or finely minced pork with fish sauce
300 g pork ribs or pork leg
20 g dried shiitake and 10 g wood ear, soaked and chopped
200 g Vietnamese pork roll (gio lua), sliced
steps: Simmer the bones and ribs in 3 litres water for 1 hour, skimming for a clear broth.
Mix the pork paste with the mushrooms and pepper and form small balls.
Drop the balls into the simmering broth and cook 6 to 8 minutes until they float and are firm.
Season, then serve over bun with ribs, gio lua slices, spring onion and cilantro.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Doc Mung (Taro Stem and Pork Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 500 g pork ribs and 500 g bones
400 g taro stems (doc mung) or celery stalks, peeled and sliced
200 g pork balls or gio song
3 tomatoes, wedged; 2 tbsp giam bong or tamarind water
steps: Simmer the ribs and bones for 1 hour; salt-scrub the taro stems and blanch 2 minutes to remove itchiness.
Fry the shallots and tomatoes until soft, then add to the broth with the vinegar.
Add the pork balls, cook 6 minutes, then the taro stems for 2 minutes so they stay spongy.
Season sour-savoury and serve over bun with ribs, dill and spring onion.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Ngan (Muscovy Duck Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 1 muscovy duck (ngan), about 2.5 kg, or regular duck
50 g bamboo shoots (mang kho), soaked and simmered
Ginger fish sauce: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp lime, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp grated ginger
steps: Rub the duck with salt and ginger, rinse, and simmer whole in 4 litres water with charred ginger and shallots for 50 minutes until cooked through.
Remove and cool the duck, chop it into pieces; add the bamboo shoots to the broth and simmer 20 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and sugar.
Serve bun in bowls with duck, bamboo, rau ram and spring onion, pour over broth and offer the ginger dipping sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mien Luon (Crispy Eel Glass Noodles)

ingredients: 500 g rice paddy eel (luon), cleaned and cut in strips
1 tbsp shredded shiitake and wood ear
Rau ram, spring onion, bean sprouts
steps: Rub the eel with salt and lime to remove slime, rinse well, and pat very dry.
Deep-fry the eel strips at 170 C for 6 to 8 minutes until shrivelled and crisp all the way through.
Bring the stock to the boil with fried shallots and mushrooms and season with fish sauce.
Blanch the soaked glass noodles for 1 minute and put in bowls; serve the crispy eel on top with herbs, and the broth either poured over or on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Da Cua (Hai Phong Crab Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 500 g rice field crabs (cua dong) or 300 g crab meat
400 g red rice noodles (banh da do) or brown flat rice noodles
200 g pork balls or fish cakes, sliced
200 g water spinach (rau muong) and 2 tbsp fried shallots
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp shrimp paste
steps: Pound the field crabs, mix with 1 litre water and strain, keeping the liquid and the crab roe.
Heat the crab liquid gently, stirring, until the crab protein rises and forms rafts; simmer 5 minutes without boiling hard, then add the stock.
Fry shallots and tomatoes and add to the soup with the pork balls; season with fish sauce and shrimp paste.
Blanch noodles and water spinach, place in bowls, add crab and toppings and ladle over the broth with fried shallots.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nem Ran (Hanoi Fried Spring Rolls)

ingredients: 150 g crab meat or chopped prawns
50 g glass noodles and 20 g wood ear, soaked and chopped
1 carrot and 1 kohlrabi, finely shredded and squeezed
2 eggs, 3 shallots minced, 1 tbsp fish sauce, pepper
Lettuce, herbs, bun and nuoc cham to serve
steps: Mix the pork, crab, noodles, mushrooms, vegetables, egg, shallots and seasoning well.
Moisten each rice paper lightly, add a spoon of filling and roll tightly, folding in the sides.
Fry in medium-hot oil (160 C) for 10 to 12 minutes until deep golden and crunchy and the filling is cooked.
Cut into pieces and serve with lettuce, herbs, bun and nuoc cham with pickled papaya.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nem Cua Be (Hai Phong Square Crab Spring Rolls)

ingredients: 400 g sea crab meat (cua be), in chunks
200 g minced pork and 150 g prawns, chopped
30 g glass noodles and wood ear, soaked and chopped
20 lattice rice papers (banh da nem luoi) or regular
Oil for frying, herbs, lettuce, bun, nuoc cham
steps: Mix the crab, pork, prawns, noodles, mushroom, carrot, egg, shallots and seasoning, keeping crab chunks visible.
Lay two rice papers crosswise, add filling and fold into a fat square parcel.
Deep-fry at 160 C for 12 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Cut each square into four and serve with herbs, bun and nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Tom Ho Tay (West Lake Shrimp Fritters)

ingredients: 150 g wheat flour, 50 g rice flour, 1 tsp turmeric
200 ml cold water, 1/2 tsp baking powder, salt
Lettuce, herbs, pickled papaya and nuoc cham
steps: Whisk flours, turmeric, baking powder, salt and water into a smooth batter and rest 10 minutes.
Toss sweet potato in batter and spread on a flat ladle, topping with 2 or 3 shrimp.
Lower into 170 C oil and fry 5 to 6 minutes until the fritter slides off and is crisp and golden.
Drain and serve hot with lettuce, herbs and nuoc cham with papaya.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Mi Que (Hai Phong Pate Baguette Sticks)

steps: Split each stick lengthways without cutting through.
Spread a thin layer of pate and a touch of butter inside and close.
Toast in a hot oven or on a grill for 4 to 5 minutes until very crisp.
Serve hot, dipped in or drizzled with chilli sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nem Chua Ran (Fried Fermented Pork Rolls)

ingredients: Chilli sauce and fresh pickled cucumber
steps: Shape the nem chua into finger-length sticks.
Dip in egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing to coat.
Fry at 170 C for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and hot right through.
Serve hot with chilli sauce and cucumber; with beer in Hanoi's street stalls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Goi (Pillow Cakes)

ingredients: 250 g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp oil, 150 ml water, salt
30 g glass noodles and wood ear, soaked and chopped
3 shallots, minced, 1 tbsp fish sauce, pepper
Lettuce, herbs, sour nuoc cham with papaya
steps: Knead the flour, baking powder, oil, salt and water into a soft dough and rest 30 minutes.
Fry the pork with shallots, noodles and mushrooms until dry, and season.
Roll the dough thin, cut circles, fill with pork and a quail egg, then fold and crimp into half-moons.
Deep-fry at 170 C for 6 to 8 minutes until puffed and golden, and serve with herbs and nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Duc Nong (Hot Rice Cake with Minced Pork)

ingredients: 200 g rice flour, 50 g tapioca starch, 1 litre water, salt
30 g wood ear, soaked and chopped
3 shallots, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp fish sauce
Thin nuoc cham broth (light fish sauce, lime, sugar, water)
steps: Soak the flours in water for 2 hours, then cook in a pot over low heat, stirring constantly, for 20 minutes until thick and translucent.
Fry shallots, pork and wood ear for 6 minutes until cooked and season.
Ladle the hot rice cake into bowls and top with pork, fried shallots and herbs.
Pour over warm thin nuoc cham and eat hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Duc Lac (Peanut Rice Cake)

ingredients: 1 tsp slaked lime water (nuoc voi trong), optional
steps: Grind the soaked rice with the water into a smooth slurry, adding lime water if using.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly for 25 minutes, until thick and glossy, then stir in the peanuts and salt.
Pour into an oiled tray, smooth and cool until set.
Cut into squares and serve with tuong dipping sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ngo Nuong (Grilled Corn)

ingredients: 4 spring onions, sliced, and 3 tbsp vegetable oil for spring onion oil (mo hanh)
1 tsp chilli flakes mixed with 1 tsp salt (muoi ot)
steps: Grill the corn over glowing charcoal, turning often, for 15 to 20 minutes until speckled brown.
Brush with spring onion oil in the last minutes.
Serve hot with chilli salt.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Xoi Xeo (Sticky Rice with Mung Bean and Fried Shallots)

ingredients: 500 g glutinous rice, soaked overnight with 1 tsp turmeric
200 g hulled mung beans, soaked 4 hours
steps: Steam the drained rice, salted, for 30 minutes, sprinkling with water halfway, until chewy.
Steam the mung beans for 20 minutes, then mash and press into a firm ball.
Fry the shallots in oil over medium heat until golden, keeping the oil.
Serve rice on banana leaf, shave mung bean over it, drizzle with shallot oil and top with crisp shallots.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Com Rang Dua Bo (Fried Rice with Pickled Greens and Beef)

ingredients: 150 g pickled mustard greens (dua chua), chopped and squeezed
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp soy sauce, spring onion
steps: Stir-fry the beef with garlic over high heat for 1 minute and set aside.
Fry the pickled greens and tomatoes for 3 minutes, season and set aside.
Fry the rice in oil over high heat until hot and separated, season with fish sauce.
Top the rice with greens and beef, toss briefly and serve with spring onion.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Chung (Square Sticky Rice Cake)

ingredients: 500 g pork belly, cut in thick strips
1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp fish sauce
20 dong leaves (la dong), or banana leaves
steps: Season the pork with salt, pepper and fish sauce for 2 hours; salt the drained rice and steam then mash the mung beans into balls.
Line a square mould with leaves, add a layer of rice, mung bean, pork, mung bean, rice, then wrap tightly and tie.
Boil the cakes submerged in water for 10 hours, topping up with boiling water.
Press under a weight overnight, then unwrap, slice and serve with pickled shallots for Tet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Gio (Pyramid Rice Dumplings)

ingredients: 200 g rice flour, 30 g tapioca starch
250 g minced pork, 30 g wood ear, 3 shallots
steps: Fry pork with shallots and wood ear until cooked and season.
Whisk the flours into the stock and cook, stirring, until a thick paste forms.
Fold banana leaves into cones, spoon in paste, add filling and a quail egg, cover with more paste and fold into pyramids.
Steam for 30 to 40 minutes until set and translucent and serve with chilli sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Day (Round Sticky Rice Cake)

ingredients: 2 tbsp toasted sesame or mung bean filling (optional)
steps: Steam the drained rice with salt for 30 minutes until fully cooked.
Pound the hot rice in a mortar until very smooth and sticky.
Oil your hands, shape into round discs and place between oiled banana leaves.
Serve with grilled or fried sides, or with sugar for a vegetarian snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cha Que (Cinnamon Pork Sausage)

ingredients: 1 kg pork paste (gio song), or lean pork pounded with fish sauce
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, pepper
steps: Mix the pork paste with cinnamon, fish sauce, sugar and pepper.
Shape into a log on banana leaves and wrap tightly, or pack around a bamboo tube.
Steam for 40 minutes, then grill over charcoal for 15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Slice and serve with rice, banh chung or sticky rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cha Com (Green Rice Pork Patties)

ingredients: 100 g young green rice flakes (com Vong)
steps: Mix the pork paste with the rice flakes and seasoning.
Shape into small flat patties.
Fry over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Serve as part of bun dau mam tom or with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Gio Thu (Pork Head Cheese)

ingredients: 1 kg pork ears, tongue and snout, cleaned
30 g wood ear, soaked and shredded
steps: Boil the pork parts for 40 minutes until tender, then slice thinly.
Fry the shallots, add pork, wood ear, pepper and fish sauce, and stir for 5 minutes.
Pack tightly in banana leaves, tie and press with a weight for 12 hours in the fridge.
Slice and serve with pickles at Tet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Dong (Jellied Pork)

steps: Blanch the pork and skin for 5 minutes and rinse.
Simmer with shallots and fish sauce for 2 hours until tender and the broth thickens.
Pour into bowls with wood ear, skim the fat and chill until set overnight.
Unmould and serve cold with pickled shallots and rice in winter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Kho Lang Vu Dai (Vu Dai Clay Pot Braised Fish)

ingredients: 1.5 kg black carp (ca tram den) or catfish steaks
100 g galangal and 50 g ginger, sliced
4 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp caramel (nuoc mau), 1 tbsp sugar
300 ml green tea or coconut water
steps: Marinate the fish with fish sauce, caramel, pepper and galangal for 1 hour.
Layer galangal, ginger and pork in a clay pot, add the fish and pour over the tea.
Simmer very gently over low heat for 10 to 12 hours, topping up if needed, until the fish is so soft the bones melt.
Serve with rice and plain boiled vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Kho Rieng (Galangal Braised Fish)

ingredients: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp caramel, 1 tsp sugar
steps: Marinate the fish with fish sauce, caramel and pepper for 20 minutes.
Line the pot with galangal, add fish and water.
Simmer gently for 50 to 60 minutes, turning once, until the sauce is thick and sticky.
Serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Vit Nau Chao (Duck Braised with Fermented Tofu)

ingredients: 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar
steps: Marinate the duck with chao, garlic, shallot and lemongrass for 30 minutes.
Fry the taro until golden and set aside.
Brown the duck in oil for 8 minutes, add liquid and simmer 40 minutes.
Add taro, cook 10 minutes more until tender and the duck is cooked through, and serve with bun or rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Oc Nhoi La Gung (Stuffed Snails Steamed in Ginger Leaves)

ingredients: 30 ginger leaves (la gung) or lime leaves
steps: Boil the snails 5 minutes, remove meat, trim and chop.
Mix snail with pork, wood ear, lemongrass and seasoning.
Stuff a ginger leaf into each shell, then fill with the mixture.
Steam for 15 to 20 minutes until cooked through and serve with ginger fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cha Muc Ha Long (Ha Long Squid Cakes)

ingredients: 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, pepper
steps: Pound the squid in a mortar until it forms a coarse sticky paste.
Mix with seasoning, starch and dill.
Shape into flat patties and fry over medium heat for 4 minutes per side until golden and springy.
Serve with sticky rice or banh cuon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cha Ruoi (Ragworm Omelette)

ingredients: 2 tbsp dill and 1 tsp tangerine zest
steps: Rinse the ruoi in warm water and drain.
Mix with pork, eggs, dill, zest and seasoning.
Fry spoonfuls in medium-hot oil for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Serve with herbs and fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: De Nui Ninh Binh (Ninh Binh Mountain Goat)

ingredients: 800 g skin-on goat meat (de nui), leg or loin
3 stalks lemongrass, 2 finely minced and 1 bruised
4 garlic cloves and 50 g ginger, minced
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
1 bunch young fig leaves (la sung), or perilla and mint as a substitute
Ginger fermented soybean sauce (tuong gung): 4 tbsp tuong, 1 tbsp grated ginger, lime, chilli
steps: Singe the goat skin over a flame until lightly charred, scrape clean and rinse.
Simmer the goat with the bruised lemongrass and half the ginger for 20 to 25 minutes until cooked through but still firm, then slice thinly.
For de xao sa, stir-fry the garlic, minced lemongrass and remaining ginger in hot oil, add the goat and seasonings, and toss over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant.
Sprinkle with sesame and serve with fig leaves to wrap each bite and the ginger tuong to dip, often with crispy rice (com chay) alongside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Com Chay Ninh Binh (Ninh Binh Crispy Rice)

ingredients: 600 g jasmine rice, cooked slightly dry
4 spring onions, sliced, and 3 tbsp oil for spring onion oil (mo hanh)
1 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp sugar (optional)
steps: Season the hot cooked rice with salt and press it firmly into a 1 cm layer on an oiled tray, then cut into squares.
Dry in the sun for a day or in an oven at 80 C for 6 to 8 hours until hard and completely dry.
Deep-fry the squares at 180 C for 30 to 60 seconds until puffed, crisp and pale golden, then drain.
Make spring onion oil by pouring hot oil over the spring onions, then drizzle over the crisps and top with pork floss; serve alongside mountain goat or as a snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau Cua Dong (Field Crab Hot Pot)

ingredients: 1 kg rice field crabs (cua dong), cleaned, or 400 g crab meat plus 1 tbsp crab paste
4 tomatoes, wedged; 4 shallots, sliced; 2 tbsp oil
2 tbsp fermented rice vinegar (giam bong) or tamarind water, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp shrimp paste
300 g beef sirloin, thinly sliced, and 200 g pork balls or fish cakes
Water spinach, banana blossom, chrysanthemum greens and mushrooms
steps: Remove the crab shells and keep the roe; pound the bodies, mix with 1 litre water and strain twice through a sieve.
Fry the shallots, the crab roe and the tomatoes in oil for 5 minutes until saucy.
Heat the crab liquid gently over medium heat, stirring once, until the crab protein rises as floating rafts; do not stir again, then add the stock, tomatoes and seasonings and simmer 10 minutes.
Bring the pot to the table on a burner and cook the beef, pork balls, tofu and vegetables in the simmering broth, making sure the meat and balls are fully cooked, and serve over bun.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Cua Rau Day (Field Crab Soup with Jute Leaves)

ingredients: 500 g rice field crabs (cua dong), cleaned, or 250 g crab meat
300 g jute leaves (rau day), or Malabar spinach (mong toi) as a substitute
To serve: salted pickled eggplant (ca phao) and plain rice
steps: Remove the crab shells and keep the roe, pound the bodies and mix with the water, then strain twice.
Heat the crab liquid over medium heat, stirring gently once or twice at first, until the crab rafts rise; then stop stirring.
Add the jute leaves and luffa and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until tender and the soup turns slightly silky; season with fish sauce and salt.
Serve as a cooling summer soup with rice and crunchy ca phao.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nom Su Hao (Kohlrabi Salad)

ingredients: 1 large kohlrabi (su hao), cut into matchsticks
150 g pork belly or prawns, boiled and thinly sliced
3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 garlic cloves and 1 chilli, minced
Vietnamese balm (kinh gioi), basil and rau ram, chopped
steps: Salt the kohlrabi and carrot for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid firmly so they stay crunchy.
Boil the pork belly for 20 minutes until cooked through (or prawns for 2 minutes), cool and slice.
Mix fish sauce, lime, sugar, garlic and chilli into a dressing.
Toss the vegetables, pork and herbs with the dressing and top with peanuts and fried shallots just before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Phao Muoi (Salted Pickled Eggplant)

ingredients: 1 kg small round white eggplants (ca phao)
4 garlic cloves, 3 chillies, 30 g ginger, sliced
steps: Remove the stems, rinse, and soak the eggplants in lightly salted water for 2 hours, then drain and dry.
Dissolve the salt and sugar in the cooled boiled water.
Pack the eggplants into a clean jar with garlic, ginger and chilli, pour over the brine and weigh down so they stay submerged.
Leave at room temperature for 3 to 5 days until crunchy and pale yellow-green, then refrigerate; serve with crab soup or mam tom.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dua Hanh (Pickled Shallots)

ingredients: 300 ml rice vinegar and 300 ml water
steps: Soak the shallots in salted water overnight or for at least 6 hours to soften the sharpness, then rinse and dry.
Boil the vinegar, water and sugar until dissolved, then cool completely.
Pack the shallots and chilli into clean jars, pour over the liquid to cover and seal.
