Keep 5 to 7 days in a cool place before eating; serve with banh chung, thit dong and other Tet dishes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Com Lang Vong (Young Green Rice Flakes)

ingredients: 300 g fresh green rice flakes (com Vong), or frozen
1 lotus leaf or banana leaf for wrapping
2 ripe bananas (chuoi ngu) or persimmons to serve
steps: Buy fresh com in autumn when it is soft, fragrant and pale green, and keep it wrapped in a lotus leaf so it does not dry out.
Loosen the flakes gently with your fingers.
Eat the com plain by the handful, with ripe banana or persimmon, or sprinkled with a little sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Com (Green Rice Flake Pudding)

ingredients: 2 tbsp tapioca starch, mixed with 3 tbsp water
1 pandan leaf, or a few drops of jasmine or grapefruit flower water
100 ml coconut milk (optional) and toasted coconut shreds
steps: Bring the water, sugar and pandan to the boil.
Stir in the starch slurry and cook 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the com and stir gently for 3 to 4 minutes until it turns soft and glossy and the pudding is thick.
Serve warm or chilled, topped with coconut milk and coconut shreds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Com (Green Rice Cake)

ingredients: 400 g hulled mung beans, soaked 4 hours
Squares of banana leaf and paper for wrapping
steps: Simmer the com with 200 g sugar and 300 ml water, stirring constantly, for 25 to 30 minutes until it forms a thick sticky green paste.
Steam the mung beans for 20 minutes, mash, then cook with the remaining sugar, oil, coconut and essence until a firm paste forms.
Flatten a portion of the green paste, place a mung bean disc in the centre, cover with more green paste and press into a square.
Wrap in banana leaf and paper and leave to firm for a few hours; serve with green tea, as made in Hang Than street.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Troi Nuoc (Floating Glutinous Rice Balls)

ingredients: 60 g palm sugar or brown sugar (duong phen), cut in small cubes
steps: Knead the flour and warm water into a smooth, soft dough that does not crack.
Pinch off small pieces, flatten, wrap each around a cube of sugar and roll into smooth balls.
Drop into a large pot of boiling water and cook until they float, then 1 to 2 minutes more.
Lift into cold water briefly, drain, toss with a little oil and serve on plates topped with sesame for the Cold Food Festival (Tet Han Thuc).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Ran (Hanoi Sesame Balls)

ingredients: 300 g glutinous rice flour and 50 g rice flour
100 g mashed potato and 50 g sugar
200 g hulled mung beans, soaked, steamed and mashed with 80 g sugar and 50 g desiccated coconut
120 g palm sugar syrup or 50 g sesame seeds
steps: Knead the flours, potato, sugar and water into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
Roll the mung bean filling into small balls and wrap each in a disc of dough, sealing well.
Fry in oil starting at 140 C and slowly raising to 170 C, pressing gently, for 10 to 12 minutes until golden and puffed.
Roll in hot palm sugar syrup for the Hanoi sweet version (or coat with sesame before frying), and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Dau Xanh Hai Duong (Mung Bean Cakes)

ingredients: 500 g hulled mung beans, soaked 4 hours
1 tsp grapefruit flower or pandan essence
steps: Steam the mung beans for 25 minutes until soft, then push through a fine sieve or blend to a smooth powder-paste.
Cook the paste with sugar, oil and salt in a non-stick pan over low heat, stirring constantly, for 15 to 20 minutes until it comes away from the pan and is crumbly-dry.
Cool, add the essence, then press tightly into small rectangular moulds.
Leave to firm in a dry place for a few hours, wrap in foil, and serve with strong green tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Phu The (Husband and Wife Cake)

ingredients: 400 ml pandan water (blend 6 pandan leaves with water and strain)
200 g hulled mung beans, steamed and mashed with 80 g sugar
1 tsp jasmine water and 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
Banana leaves folded into small square boxes
steps: Mix the tapioca starch, pandan water, sugar and coconut and rest 30 minutes.
Cook over low heat, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes until just thickening.
Spoon a layer into each banana-leaf box, add a ball of mung bean filling and cover with more batter; sprinkle with sesame.
Steam for 20 minutes until clear and set, then cool and serve in their leaf boxes, traditional at Dinh Bang weddings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Phe Trung (Hanoi Egg Coffee)

ingredients: 120 ml strong hot Vietnamese drip coffee (made with a phin filter)
steps: Use pasteurised eggs because the yolk is not cooked, and brew the coffee in a phin directly into small cups kept warm in a bowl of hot water.
Whisk the yolks, condensed milk, sugar and vanilla with an electric whisk for 5 to 6 minutes until thick, pale and creamy like a meringue.
Spoon the foam over the hot coffee and serve at once with a teaspoon, Giang cafe style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tra Sen (Lotus Tea)

ingredients: 10 g green tea scented with lotus (tra sen Tay Ho), from a tea shop
steps: Rinse the teapot and cups with boiling water to warm them.
Add the tea, pour over a little water at 85 C, swirl and discard to rinse the leaves.
Refill with 85 C water, steep 1 to 2 minutes and pour into small cups; the tea should smell sweetly of lotus.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tra Chanh (Hanoi Lime Iced Tea)

ingredients: 2 tsp jasmine or green tea leaves
steps: Steep the tea in 85 C water for 3 minutes, strain and cool.
Shake the tea with lime juice, syrup and plenty of ice.
Pour into glasses with a lime slice and drink on low plastic stools by the cathedral with sunflower seeds.

dishes.name: Bia Hoi (Fresh Draught Beer)

ingredients: 2 litres fresh bia hoi, bought from a licensed brewery outlet or bia hoi stall
Snacks: roasted peanuts, nem chua ran, grilled dried squid
steps: Bia hoi is a light, low-alcohol, unpasteurised lager brewed daily and delivered to street corners in kegs; it is meant to be drunk the same day.
Buy it from a licensed brewer or bia hoi stall and serve it cold in thick glass mugs, sometimes over ice.
Drink it at a street-side bia hoi with peanuts, fried fermented pork and grilled squid; this is an adults-only drink.

dishes.name: Thang Co (Hmong Horse Meat Stew)

ingredients: 1 kg horse meat and mixed horse offal (heart, liver, tripe, lung), cleaned (beef shin and beef offal are the usual substitute)
2 tbsp thao qua (black cardamom), toasted and crushed
1 tbsp hat mac khen (Sichuan-style prickly ash seeds), toasted and crushed
1 thumb ginger, sliced, plus 4 stalks lemongrass, bruised
2 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tsp salt
2 tbsp neutral oil or pork lard
To serve: cham cheo dipping salt, fresh chili, Vietnamese coriander, corn wine on the side
steps: Rub the meat and offal well with salt and ginger, rinse several times, then blanch everything in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain to remove impurities; cut into bite-size pieces.
Grind the toasted cardamom, mac khen, star anise, cinnamon and fennel into a coarse powder and toss half of it with the meat, fish sauce and lemongrass; leave 30 minutes.
Heat the lard in a large heavy pot over high heat and stir-fry the seasoned meat for 8-10 minutes until it releases its juices and the fat starts to sizzle again.
Pour in the water, add the remaining spice powder, bring to a boil, skim, and simmer covered on low heat for 2.5-3 hours until the tripe and meat are fully tender.
Taste and adjust with salt or fish sauce, then serve the stew bubbling in a wide pot at the table with cham cheo, chilies and herbs, as at Hmong highland markets.

dishes.name: Lon Cap Nach (Grilled Hill Pig)

ingredients: 1 kg lon cap nach (small free-range hill pig) leg or shoulder with skin on (skin-on pork shoulder works)
2 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash seeds), toasted and ground
1 tsp hat doi (doi seeds), toasted and ground (or extra black pepper)
4 cloves garlic, minced, and 2 shallots, minced
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tsp salt
To serve: cham cheo dipping salt, sliced cucumber, wild herbs
steps: Scrape the pork skin clean, briefly singe it over a flame, rinse and pat dry; score the meat in a crisscross to let the marinade in.
Mix the mac khen, hat doi, garlic, shallot, lemongrass, fish sauce, salt and lard and rub it all over the meat side; marinate for at least 1 hour.
Grill over medium charcoal for about 50-60 minutes, turning often and keeping it high off the coals so it cooks through before the skin burns; the juices should run clear and the centre reach 71°C.
In the last 10 minutes brush the skin with honey thinned with a little water and grill skin-side down until blistered and amber.
Rest 5 minutes, slice thinly and serve with cham cheo, cucumber and herbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Thit Trau Gac Bep (Smoked Buffalo Jerky)

ingredients: 1 kg buffalo topside or rump, trimmed of fat (lean beef works)
2 tbsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash), toasted and ground
1 tbsp hat doi seeds, toasted and ground (or black pepper)
To serve: cham cheo dipping salt or chili salt
steps: Cut the buffalo along the grain into strips about 3 cm thick and 20 cm long.
Mix all the spices, ginger, lemongrass, salt, sugar and fish sauce and rub thoroughly into the strips; cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.

Traditionally the strips hang above the kitchen hearth (gac bep) for days; at home, smoke at 70-80°C over wood chips or dry in a low oven at 75°C with the door slightly ajar for 3-4 hours until dark and firm right through.
Store dried strips airtight in the fridge; to serve, steam for 10 minutes or warm over charcoal, then pound lightly with a pestle and tear into fibres.
Serve the torn fibres with cham cheo and a glass of tea or corn wine.

dishes.name: Thit Lon Gac Bep (Smoked Pork)

ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder or belly, skin on
2 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash), toasted and ground
1 tsp hat doi seeds, ground (or black pepper)
1 tbsp grated ginger and 3 cloves garlic, minced
To serve: cham cheo, sliced cucumber
steps: Cut the pork into long strips about 4 cm wide, keeping a strip of skin on each.
Rub with the spices, ginger, garlic, chili, salt, sugar and corn wine and marinate overnight in the fridge.
Smoke at 70-80°C over hardwood (or dry in a 75°C oven) for about 4 hours until the outside is dark and dry; hill families hang it over the hearth for weeks.
Before eating, steam for 20-25 minutes until fully hot and cooked through, or grill over embers until the fat crackles.
Slice thinly across the grain and serve with cham cheo and cucumber.

dishes.name: Xoi Ngu Sac (Five-colour Sticky Rice)

ingredients: 1 kg glutinous rice (gao nep), split into 5 portions of 200 g
1 handful la cam (magenta plant leaves) for purple/red (or butterfly pea plus lime for violet)
1 thumb fresh turmeric (nghe), grated, for yellow
1 handful pandan or la riem leaves, blended, for green
1 handful dried la chit (black colour leaves) or 1 tbsp activated charcoal powder for black
4 tbsp grated coconut or roasted sesame with salt, to serve
steps: Boil the la cam leaves in 500 ml water for 10 minutes and strain; blend pandan with 300 ml water and strain; mix turmeric with 300 ml water; soak la chit leaves in hot water for black.
Soak each 200 g portion of rice in its own colour liquid (one portion in plain water stays white) overnight, adding a pinch of salt to each.
Drain each portion and steam them in separate sections of a cloth-lined steamer over high heat for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle 2 tbsp water over the rice, toss gently, and steam another 10-15 minutes until every grain is glossy and tender.
Arrange the five colours side by side on a banana leaf and serve with sesame salt or coconut, as the Tay and Thai do for festivals.

dishes.name: Xoi Tu Le (Tu Le Sticky Rice)

ingredients: 600 g Tu Le glutinous rice (nep Tu Le, from Yen Bai) or any fragrant long-grain glutinous rice
1 tsp salt for the sesame salt
2 tbsp pork lard or oil, warmed
steps: Rinse the rice and soak overnight in cool water with 1 tsp salt.
Drain well and steam in a cloth-lined steamer over high heat for 25 minutes.
Turn the rice into a bowl, toss with the warm lard and a sprinkle of water, then steam again for 10-15 minutes until soft, sticky and very fragrant.
Grind the sesame lightly with 1 tsp salt to make muoi vung.
Wrap portions in banana leaves and serve with sesame salt and coconut, the way Thai women sell it in the Tu Le valley.

dishes.name: Com Lam (Bamboo Tube Rice)

ingredients: 4 sections fresh young bamboo (tre or nua), 30-40 cm, one end closed by a node (or banana leaves rolled in foil)
400 ml water or thin coconut milk
4 pieces banana leaf or dong leaf, to plug the tubes
To serve: toasted sesame salt and grilled meat
steps: Soak the rice in salted water for 4 hours, then drain.
Fill each bamboo tube about two-thirds with rice, add water or coconut milk to just cover, and plug the open end tightly with a rolled leaf.
Lay the tubes over medium charcoal or a wood fire, turning every few minutes, for 45-60 minutes until the outside is charred and you hear the liquid stop bubbling.
Let cool 10 minutes, then peel or split away the charred bamboo to leave a cylinder of rice wrapped in the thin inner membrane.
Slice into rounds and serve with sesame salt, or alongside grilled pork or chicken.

dishes.name: Pa Pinh Top (Thai Folded Grilled Fish)

ingredients: 2 whole carp or tilapia (about 600 g each), scaled and gutted
2 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash), toasted and ground
1 thumb ginger and 1 thumb galangal, finely chopped
3 cloves garlic and 3 fresh chilies, chopped
1 handful rau mui tau (sawtooth coriander), ngo om and spring onion, chopped
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tsp salt
To serve: sticky rice and cham cheo
steps: Split each fish open along the back (not the belly) so it opens like a book, keeping the belly side joined; rinse and pat dry.
Pound the lemongrass, ginger, galangal, garlic and chili into a coarse paste and mix with the herbs, mac khen, fish sauce, salt and oil.
Stuff the paste into the opened fish, fold it closed (pa pinh top means folded grilled fish), and clamp each fish in a split bamboo or wire grill rack.
Grill over medium charcoal for 12-15 minutes per side until the skin is crisp and the flesh flakes and is opaque to the bone.
Serve whole with sticky rice and cham cheo, as the Thai of Son La and Dien Bien do.

dishes.name: Ca Suoi Nuong (Grilled Stream Fish)

ingredients: 600 g small stream fish (ca suoi), scaled and gutted (or small trout, smelt or sardines)
1 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash), ground
2 cloves garlic, minced, and 2 chilies, minced
To serve: cham cheo, sticky rice and wild herbs
steps: Rinse the fish, keep them whole, and pat dry.
Mix the lemongrass, garlic, chili, mac khen, salt, sugar and oil and rub it over and inside the fish; rest 15 minutes.
Thread the fish onto bamboo skewers or clamp them in a grill rack.
Grill over medium-hot charcoal for 6-8 minutes per side until crisp and golden and the flesh flakes easily.
Serve hot with cham cheo, sticky rice and herbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nam Pia (Thai Cattle Offal Soup)

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef or goat offal (tripe, intestines, liver, heart, lungs, meat trimmings), thoroughly cleaned
200 g pia (cooked contents of the cow's small intestine, sold by Thai cooks in Son La); it is optional and can be left out
2 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash), toasted and ground
1 thumb ginger and 1 thumb galangal, sliced
1 handful herbs: sawtooth coriander, Vietnamese coriander, spring onion
1 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp fish sauce
steps: Clean the offal with salt and lime, rinse well, blanch for 5 minutes in boiling water and drain; cut into small pieces.
Put the offal in a pot with the water, lemongrass, ginger, galangal, garlic and chilies, bring to a boil and skim.
Simmer on low heat for about 2 hours until the tripe and intestines are tender; if using pia, stir it in for the last 20 minutes and keep boiling hard so it is fully cooked.
Season with salt, fish sauce and mac khen; the broth should be bitter-spicy and peppery.
Ladle into bowls, top with the chopped herbs, and serve with sticky rice and corn wine, as a Thai feast dish of the Northwest.

dishes.name: Cham Cheo (Northwest Chili Dipping Salt)

ingredients: 2 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash seeds) (or Sichuan peppercorns)
1 tsp hat doi seeds (or black pepper)
6 fresh red chilies, grilled until blistered
1 handful sawtooth coriander (rau mui tau) and Vietnamese coriander
2 tbsp warm water or lime juice
steps: Toast the mac khen and hat doi seeds in a dry pan over low heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant, then grind to a powder.
Pound the grilled chilies, garlic and salt in a mortar to a coarse paste.
Add the chopped herbs and pound briefly, then mix in the ground spices and MSG or sugar.
Loosen with warm water or lime juice and serve as the all-purpose dip for grilled meats, sticky rice, boiled vegetables and smoked buffalo.

dishes.name: Men Men (Hmong Steamed Ground Maize)

ingredients: 500 g dried white or yellow corn, coarsely milled (or coarse cornmeal/polenta)
200 ml water, plus more for sprinkling
To serve: vegetable soup (canh rau cai) and chili salt
steps: Sprinkle the milled corn with the water and salt, mixing with your hands until every grain is damp but still loose; leave 1 hour.
Rub the damp corn through your fingers to break up lumps, then put it in a cloth-lined steamer (the Hmong use a wooden steamer, chõ).
Steam over high heat for 20 minutes, tip out, sprinkle with a little water, rub loose again and steam a second time for 15-20 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Toss with lard if using and serve hot with mustard-green soup and chili salt, the everyday staple of the Ha Giang Hmong.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Tam Giac Mach (Buckwheat Cake)

ingredients: 300 g buckwheat flour (bot tam giac mach)
steps: Mix the buckwheat flour, rice flour, sugar or honey and salt, then add the warm water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide into 8 pieces and press each into a round cake about 1.5 cm thick.
Steam the cakes over high heat for 15 minutes until firm.
Grill over charcoal or dry-fry in a lightly oiled pan for 3-4 minutes per side until speckled and toasty.
Serve warm, drizzled with honey, as sold at the Dong Van and Meo Vac markets.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chao Au Tau (Ha Giang Aconite Root Porridge)

ingredients: 200 g dried Chinese yam (hoai son), soaked 1 hour — the safe home substitute for au tau root
4 pork trotters (chan gio), cut into chunks
150 g ordinary rice and 50 g glutinous rice
1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp fish sauce
To serve: spring onion, herbs, ground pepper, a raw egg yolk per bowl (optional)
steps: Important: real au tau is aconite root, which is highly poisonous unless detoxified by specialist cooks, and has caused deaths. Do not prepare it at home — enjoy the genuine dish only from established porridge shops in Ha Giang. This home version uses Chinese yam for the same soft, floury texture.
Blanch the trotters, then simmer them in 2 l water for 1.5-2 hours until tender, skimming.
Simmer the soaked yam in a little of the broth for 20 minutes until soft, then mash it.
Add the rinsed rice and mashed yam to the trotter broth and cook on low heat, stirring often, for 45-60 minutes until thick and smooth; season with salt and fish sauce.
Serve hot with a trotter piece, spring onion and pepper; stir in an egg yolk if liked (the hot porridge will cook it).

dishes.name: Thang Den (Ha Giang Floating Rice Dumplings)

ingredients: 80 g split mung beans, cooked and mashed with 1 tbsp sugar
150 g palm sugar or dark brown sugar
2 tbsp roasted peanuts and 1 tbsp toasted sesame
steps: Knead the rice flour and warm water into a soft dough; pinch into balls the size of a walnut and fill each with a little mung bean paste, rolling smooth.
Simmer the palm sugar and ginger in 500 ml water for 10 minutes to make a fragrant syrup.
Drop the dumplings into a pot of boiling water; once they float (about 4-5 minutes), cook 1 minute more and lift them into cool water.
Ladle dumplings into bowls with the warm ginger syrup, a spoon of coconut milk, peanuts and sesame; this is the warming winter street sweet of Ha Giang.

dishes.name: Banh Cuon Cao Bang (Cao Bang Rice Rolls in Bone Broth)

ingredients: 300 g rice flour batter base: 300 g long-grain rice soaked overnight and blended with 600 ml water (or 250 g rice flour + 30 g tapioca starch + 650 ml water)
4 wood ear mushrooms, soaked and finely chopped
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tsp salt
To serve: spring onion, cha lua slices, chili
steps: Simmer the pork bones in 2 l water for 1.5 hours, skimming, then season with salt and fish sauce to make a clear hot broth (Cao Bang rolls are eaten in broth, not fish sauce).
Stir-fry the shallot, pork and wood ear in oil over high heat for 5 minutes until cooked; season with a little fish sauce.
Stretch a cloth over a pot of boiling water, ladle on a thin layer of batter, cover 30-40 seconds until translucent, add filling (or crack an egg on top and spread it), then lift and roll.
Place the rolls in bowls, ladle the boiling bone broth over, and top with spring onion, fried shallots and a slice of cha lua.

dishes.name: Banh Coong Phu (Tay Sweet Rice Ball Soup)

ingredients: 120 g mung bean paste or a lump of brown sugar per ball
150 g brown cane sugar (duong phen or mat mia)
steps: Knead the rice flour and water into a soft dough and shape walnut-size balls, filling each with mung bean paste or a piece of sugar.
Boil the cane sugar and ginger in 600 ml water for 10 minutes into a light syrup.
Cook the balls in boiling water until they float, then 1 minute more, and transfer into the ginger syrup to simmer for 3 minutes.
Serve warm, sprinkled with sesame; the Tay of Cao Bang make it for the Cold Food festival and family gatherings.

dishes.name: Hat De Trung Khanh (Roasted Trung Khanh Chestnuts)

ingredients: 500 g Trung Khanh chestnuts (hat de, from Cao Bang) or other sweet chestnuts
1 kg coarse salt or clean sand, for roasting
steps: Rinse and dry the chestnuts, then cut a small slit in the shell of each so they do not burst.
Heat the salt in a wok over medium heat for 5 minutes until very hot.
Bury the chestnuts in the salt and stir continuously for 20-25 minutes until the shells darken and open and the flesh is soft and floury.
Sprinkle with sugar in the last 2 minutes if you like a glaze, then sift out the salt and serve hot in paper cones.

dishes.name: Vit Quay Lang Son (Mac Mat Leaf Roast Duck)

ingredients: 1 large handful la mac mat (Clausena leaves) (or makrut lime leaves plus a little curry leaf)
4 cloves garlic, 3 shallots and 1 thumb ginger, minced
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt
1 tbsp fermented tofu or red fermented bean curd (optional)
3 tbsp honey mixed with 2 tbsp rice vinegar
To serve: the cavity juices as sauce, cucumber, herbs
steps: Mix the garlic, shallot, ginger, five-spice, fish sauce, sugar, salt and fermented tofu, then stuff it with the mac mat leaves into the duck cavity and sew it closed.
Pour boiling water over the skin to tighten it, pat dry, brush with the honey-vinegar mix and air-dry for at least 1 hour (or overnight in the fridge).
Roast over charcoal on a rotisserie or in a 200°C oven for about 80-90 minutes, basting with honey every 20 minutes, until the skin is lacquered and crisp and the thigh juices run clear.
Rest 10 minutes, tip the cavity juices into a bowl as the sauce, chop the duck and serve with cucumber and herbs, a classic of Lang Son markets.

dishes.name: Lon Quay Lang Son (Mac Mat Leaf Roast Pork)

ingredients: 2 kg pork belly or a boned shoulder, skin on, in one piece
1 large handful la mac mat (Clausena leaves) (or makrut lime leaves)
4 cloves garlic, 3 shallots and 1 thumb ginger, minced
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt
3 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp rice vinegar
To serve: cucumber, herbs and soy-chili dip
steps: Prick the skin all over with a fork or skewer, pour boiling water over it and pat dry.

Rub the meat side (not the skin) with garlic, shallot, ginger, five-spice, bean curd, fish sauce, sugar and salt; lay the mac mat leaves over the meat, roll or fold the pork around them and tie with string.
Brush the skin with honey-vinegar and leave uncovered in the fridge for at least 1 hour to dry.
Roast over charcoal or at 180°C for 1.5 hours, then raise the heat to 230°C for 20-30 minutes until the skin crackles and the internal temperature is at least 71°C.
Rest 15 minutes, chop into pieces and serve with cucumber, herbs and dip.

dishes.name: Khau Nhuc (Tay Steamed Pork Belly with Taro)

ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, skin on, in one slab
500 g taro (khoai mon), peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
2 tbsp fermented tofu (chao) or red bean curd
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt
1 handful mac mat leaves or makrut lime leaves (optional)
steps: Boil the pork belly whole for 25 minutes until just cooked, then prick the skin, brush it with honey and fry skin-down in hot oil (carefully, cover with a lid) for 5 minutes until blistered and golden.
Cut the pork into slices 1 cm thick and marinate with garlic, shallot, five-spice, fermented tofu, fish sauce, sugar and salt for 30 minutes.
Fry the taro slices in the same oil for 4-5 minutes until golden on the edges.
In a deep bowl, layer pork slices (skin down) alternating with taro and mac mat leaves, pour over the leftover marinade, and steam over medium heat for 1.5-2 hours until the pork is meltingly soft.
Invert the bowl onto a plate so the glossy skin is on top and serve with rice, as the Tay and Nung do at weddings.

dishes.name: Pho Chua Lang Son (Lang Son Sour Pho)

ingredients: 500 g fresh wide rice noodles (banh pho), blanched
200 g roast pork or roast duck (Lang Son style), sliced
100 g pork liver and gizzards, boiled and sliced (optional)
2 tbsp roasted peanuts and 1 handful fried taro or sweet potato strips
1 cucumber and 1 small green papaya, julienned
Sauce: 4 tbsp rice vinegar, 3 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp roast-meat juices, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp tapioca starch, 150 ml water
2 cloves garlic, minced, and 1 tsp chili sauce
1 handful herbs: Vietnamese coriander, mint, basil
steps: Cook the sauce ingredients and garlic over low heat, stirring, until it simmers and thickens slightly; it should be sweet-sour and glossy, then let cool.
Put the noodles in bowls and arrange roast meat, offal, cucumber, papaya and herbs on top.
Pour the cooled sour sauce over each bowl.
Finish with fried taro strips, peanuts and chili, and toss at the table; it is served room-temperature, not as soup.

dishes.name: Lau Ca Hoi Sa Pa (Sapa Salmon Hot Pot)

ingredients: 1 kg salmon or rainbow trout from Sa Pa farms: head and bones for broth, fillet sliced
2 tomatoes and 1 pineapple slice, cut into wedges
2 tbsp tamarind paste or 2 tbsp mang chua (sour bamboo shoots)
2 stalks lemongrass and 1 thumb ginger, crushed
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp sugar
300 g vegetables: cai meo (Hmong mustard), chayote shoots (ngon su su), mushrooms
steps: Grill or briefly fry the salmon head and bones, then simmer them with lemongrass, ginger and 1.5 l water for 40 minutes; strain.
Fry the shallots in oil, add tomatoes and pineapple and cook 3 minutes, then add to the broth with tamarind; season with fish sauce, salt and sugar to a sour-savoury taste.
Bring the broth to a boil on a table burner and add dill and spring onion.
Diners dip salmon slices and vegetables into the boiling broth for 1-2 minutes until the fish turns opaque, eating them with vermicelli and chili-fish-sauce dip.

dishes.name: Be Chao Moc Chau (Moc Chau Sauteed Veal)

ingredients: 500 g veal (be) leg or loin from Moc Chau, thinly sliced
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp ground pepper
1 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash), ground (optional)
To serve: la mo (Paederia leaves) or Vietnamese coriander, ginger-lemongrass-fermented tofu dip (tuong gung)
steps: Marinate the veal with half the garlic and lemongrass, fish sauce, sugar, pepper and mac khen for 15 minutes.
Heat the lard in a wok over the highest heat until smoking and fry the remaining garlic and lemongrass for 20 seconds.
Add the veal and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just browned on the outside and cooked through (no pink juices); add ginger in the last 30 seconds.
Serve immediately with herbs and the ginger-fermented-tofu dip, as at Moc Chau plateau inns.

dishes.name: Nom Hoa Ban (Bauhinia Flower Salad)

ingredients: 300 g white hoa ban (bauhinia) flowers, stamens removed (or banana blossom, finely shredded)
100 g smoked dried stream fish (ca suoi kho) or smoked pork, shredded
2 tbsp roasted sesame or peanuts, crushed
1 tsp mac khen (mountain prickly ash), ground
1 handful sawtooth coriander and Vietnamese coriander, chopped
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp lime juice
steps: Blanch the flowers in boiling salted water for 30 seconds, plunge into cold water and squeeze dry.
Grill the dried fish briefly over flame until fragrant, then shred the flesh, discarding bones.
Pound the garlic, chili and mac khen, then mix with fish sauce, salt and lime juice.
Toss the flowers with the fish, dressing and herbs, then finish with sesame; the Thai make this in spring when bauhinia blooms across Son La and Dien Bien.

dishes.name: Ruou Ngo (Hmong Corn Wine)

ingredients: 400 ml ruou ngo Ban Pho or other Hmong corn wine, bought from a licensed producer
4 small cups or a gourd ladle
1 plate smoked meat or thang co, to accompany
steps: Ruou ngo is a strong clear spirit distilled from fermented corn by the Hmong of Ha Giang and Lao Cai (Ban Pho village in Bac Ha is the most famous); buy it from licensed producers only.
Serve it at room temperature in small cups, poured from a jug or gourd, alongside thang co, smoked buffalo or grilled meat at markets and festivals.
Drink slowly in small sips with food; it is customary to toast together with every round.

dishes.name: Ruou Tao Meo (Wild Apple Wine)

ingredients: 400 ml ruou tao meo (wild Docynia apple wine) from Mu Cang Chai or Sa Pa, bought from a licensed producer
1 plate sliced fresh or dried tao meo, to accompany (optional)
steps: Ruou tao meo is a rice spirit in which the small, tart wild apples of the Northwest (Docynia indica) are steeped for months, giving an amber colour and sour-sweet fruit aroma; buy it bottled from licensed producers.
Serve slightly chilled or at room temperature in small glasses.
Offer it with grilled meats or after the meal; the dried apple slices make a good tart snack beside it.

dishes.name: Tra Thai Nguyen (Thai Nguyen Green Tea)

ingredients: 10 g Thai Nguyen green tea (che Tan Cuong), tightly rolled leaves
4 small tea cups and a small clay pot
steps: Bring the water to a boil and let it cool to about 85-90°C.
Warm the teapot and cups with hot water and discard it, then add the tea and rinse it with a splash of hot water, pouring that away immediately.
Fill the pot with the 85-90°C water, cover and steep 1-2 minutes until pale green-gold.
Pour into small cups and sip without sugar, refilling the pot for 3-4 more infusions; it is grassy, slightly astringent, with a sweet aftertaste (ngot hau).

dishes.name: Nem Chua Thanh Hoa (Thanh Hoa Fermented Pork)

ingredients: 500 g very fresh lean pork leg, minced finely, from a trusted inspected source
150 g cooked pork skin, cut into thin strips
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp salt, 2 tsp sugar
6 garlic cloves, sliced, and 6 bird's eye chillies
1 tsp curing salt (with nitrite) per the packet dose, recommended for safety
Guava leaves (la oi) or chilli leaves, and banana leaves
steps: Pound the minced pork until sticky, then mix in the pork skin, thinh, seasonings and curing salt very thoroughly with clean gloves.
Shape into small blocks, press a garlic slice and a piece of chilli onto each, wrap in a guava leaf and then tightly in banana leaf.
Leave at about 25 to 30 C for 3 days until firm, pinkish and pleasantly sour, then refrigerate.

Traditionally eaten raw as a fermented food; for safety many cooks grill the wrapped nem over charcoal for 10 minutes or fry it (see nem chua ran), and it should not be served raw to children, pregnant people or the elderly; easiest is to buy factory-made Thanh Hoa nem.

dishes.name: Goi Nhech Nga Son (Nga Son Raw Eel Salad)

ingredients: 500 g very fresh small sea eels (ca nhech) or loach, filleted
50 g galangal and 30 g ginger, finely shredded
Sauce: 4 tbsp tuong, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp galangal, cooked down with 2 tbsp minced pork
A large plate of leaves: guava, fig (la sung), perilla, mint, lettuce
steps: Rub the eel with salt and lime to remove slime, rinse, and fillet into thin slivers.
Because freshwater and brackish eel can carry parasites, blanch the slivers in boiling water for 30 to 45 seconds until opaque, then drain; the traditional raw version is not recommended.
Toss the eel with lime juice, galangal, ginger, garlic and chilli for 10 minutes, then squeeze out and mix with roasted rice powder.
Simmer the tuong sauce ingredients for 5 minutes until thick, and serve the salad wrapped in mixed leaves with the sauce for dipping.

dishes.name: Banh Gai Tu Tru (Ramie Leaf Sticky Cake)

ingredients: 200 g dried ramie leaves (la gai), boiled and pounded, or 2 tbsp ramie leaf powder
300 g hulled mung beans, steamed and mashed with 80 g sugar
100 g grated coconut and 50 g candied winter melon (mut bi)
1 tbsp oil and dried banana leaves for wrapping
steps: Cook the pounded ramie leaves with the sugar over low heat until thick, then knead with the glutinous rice flour and oil into a smooth black dough.
Mix the mung bean, coconut and winter melon into a filling and roll into balls.
Wrap each filling ball in dough, roll in sesame and wrap tightly in dried banana leaves.
Steam for 60 to 90 minutes until the dough is translucent and chewy, then cool before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chao Luon Nghe An (Nghe An Eel Porridge)

ingredients: 500 g rice paddy eel (luon), cleaned with salt and lime
150 g rice, toasted dry in a pan
3 shallots, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp minced lemongrass, 2 tbsp oil
2 tbsp fish sauce, black pepper and chilli
Vietnamese mint (rau ram), spring onion and bun or fried bread sticks (banh mi or quay)
steps: Boil the eels for 5 minutes until cooked, take the meat off the bones and return the bones to the pot with the rice and water.
Simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until the rice grains are soft but still visible.
Fry the eel meat with shallots, turmeric and lemongrass for 5 minutes until fragrant and season with fish sauce.
Ladle porridge into bowls, top with the eel, plenty of black pepper, chilli, rau ram and spring onion, and serve with bread sticks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sup Luon Vinh (Vinh Eel Soup)

ingredients: 600 g rice paddy eels, cleaned with salt and lime
1 tsp turmeric, 2 tbsp minced lemongrass, 4 shallots
2 chillies, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar
Rau ram, spring onion, banh mi or banh duc to dip
steps: Boil the eels for 5 minutes, then remove the meat in strips; simmer the bones in the stock for 20 minutes and strain.
Fry the eel with shallots, turmeric, lemongrass and chilli for 5 minutes until fragrant and well browned.
Add the eel to the stock, season with fish sauce and sugar and simmer 5 minutes; the soup should be rich, yellow and peppery.
Serve with rau ram, spring onion and bread or banh duc to dunk.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Muot Nghe An (Nghe An Rice Sheets with Chicken)

ingredients: 600 g fresh thin rice sheets (banh muot), or uncut fresh pho sheets as substitute
Nuoc cham with ginger and lime, rau ram, chilli
steps: Simmer the chicken with ginger and shallots for 35 minutes until the juices run clear, then cool and shred.
Steam the rice sheets for 1 minute to soften, fold into bundles and brush with spring onion oil.
Top with shredded chicken and fried shallots.
Serve with warm ginger nuoc cham and herbs, or with a small bowl of the chicken broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nhut Thanh Chuong (Pickled Young Jackfruit)

ingredients: 2 kg young unripe jackfruit, or canned young green jackfruit in brine
steps: Oil your hands, peel the jackfruit and cut into thin slivers, soaking them in salted water for 1 hour to remove sap.
Squeeze dry, then pack firmly into a clean jar with garlic, chilli and lemongrass.
Dissolve the salt in the water, pour over to cover, and weigh down.
Leave 5 to 7 days until sour and crunchy, then refrigerate; serve as a side, or stir-fried with pork or cooked with fish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tuong Nam Dan (Nam Dan Fermented Soybean Paste)

ingredients: 500 g bought tuong Nam Dan, or Vietnamese fermented soybean paste (tuong ban)
steps: Tuong Nam Dan is made by fermenting toasted soybeans and glutinous rice mould in salt brine in clay jars in the sun for months; buy it ready-made from a producer or Asian shop.
For a dipping sauce, fry the garlic in oil, add 6 tbsp tuong and the sugar, and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in ginger, chilli and lime off the heat.
Serve with boiled vegetables, boiled pork, rice and goat dishes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nuoc Che Xanh (Fresh Green Tea Leaf Brew)

ingredients: 150 g fresh green tea leaves and young stems (che tuoi), or 30 g whole-leaf green tea
steps: Wash the leaves, then crush them lightly in your hands.
Rinse them in boiling water and discard the water.
Pack into a teapot or pot, pour over fresh boiling water and steep 10 to 15 minutes until deep green-yellow; drink hot from bowls, Nghe An village style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cu Do Ha Tinh (Ginger Peanut Molasses Candy)

ingredients: 300 g sugarcane molasses or dark palm sugar (mat mia)
12 thin toasted rice crackers (banh da vung), with sesame
steps: Simmer the molasses with ginger and maltose over low heat, stirring, for 20 to 30 minutes until a drop on a cold plate sets chewy.
Stir in the peanuts and keep stirring 5 minutes until the mixture pulls together.
Spread a thick layer of the hot candy onto a rice cracker, top with another cracker and press.
Cool, cut into wedges and serve with nuoc che xanh.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ram Ha Tinh (Ha Tinh Mini Spring Rolls)

ingredients: 30 g wood ear and 30 g glass noodles, soaked and chopped
40 small thin rice papers (banh da Ha Tinh) or regular rice paper cut in quarters
Oil for frying, lettuce, herbs and sweet nuoc cham
steps: Mix the pork, shrimp, wood ear, noodles, shallots, egg and seasoning.
Roll a small spoonful tightly in each rice paper, making finger-sized rolls.
Fry at 170 C for 6 to 8 minutes until blistered, crisp and the filling is cooked.
Serve with lettuce, herbs and a sweet-spicy nuoc cham, wrapped together.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chao Canh Quang Binh (Quang Binh Thick Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 400 g rice flour mixed with 50 g tapioca starch and 300 ml hot water, or 600 g fresh banh canh noodles
300 g shrimp or pork (or snakehead fish), cooked
3 shallots, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp annatto or paprika for colour
steps: Simmer the bones in 2 litres water for 45 minutes and strain.
Knead the flour dough, roll thin and cut into thick noodles, or use fresh banh canh.
Fry shallots with annatto, add the shrimp or pork and fish sauce, cook 3 minutes, and add to the broth.
Drop in the noodles and simmer 5 to 7 minutes until they turn soft and the broth thickens; serve with spring onion, pepper and chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Khoai Deo Quang Binh (Chewy Dried Sweet Potato)

ingredients: Clean drying racks or oven trays
1 tsp vegetable oil for the trays
steps: Wash the sweet potatoes and steam or boil whole for 45 to 60 minutes until fully soft.
Peel while warm and slice into 1 cm strips.
Dry in the sun for 2 to 3 days or in an oven at 60 C for 10 to 12 hours, turning, until chewy and translucent.
Store airtight and eat as a snack, lightly warmed over charcoal if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Canh Ca Loc (Snakehead Fish Thick Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 600 g snakehead fish (ca loc), or tilapia
600 g fresh thick rice-tapioca noodles (banh canh)
4 shallots, 1 tsp annatto oil, 2 tbsp oil
2 tbsp fish sauce, black pepper, chilli
steps: Simmer the bones 45 minutes; poach the fish in the stock for 10 minutes until it flakes, lift out and remove skin and bones.
Fry shallots with annatto, add the fish flakes and fish sauce, and cook 3 minutes.
Add the noodles to the broth and simmer 5 minutes until tender and slightly thickened; add the fish.
Serve with spring onion, rau ram, black pepper and chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Bo Hue (Spicy Hue Beef Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 1 kg beef shank (bap bo), plus 1 kg pork and beef bones
4 pork knuckle slices (gio heo), about 600 g
6 stalks lemongrass, bruised, plus 2 stalks finely minced
2 tbsp mam ruoc Hue (fermented shrimp paste), dissolved in 200 ml water and settled
2 tbsp annatto oil with 2 tbsp chili flakes and 2 cloves minced garlic (sate oil)
3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp rock sugar and 1 tsp salt
200 g cha Hue (Hue pork sausage), sliced
800 g thick round rice noodles (bun bo Hue / bun so 3), cooked
To serve: shredded banana blossom, water spinach, mint, lime, chili
steps: Blanch the bones, beef shank and pork knuckle for 5 minutes, rinse, then put them in 4 l fresh water with the bruised lemongrass and charred onion.
Simmer gently, skimming; remove the shank after 1.5 hours and the knuckle after 2 hours when tender, and keep the bones simmering for another hour.
Strain the settled shrimp paste liquid into the broth (leave the sediment behind) and season with fish sauce, rock sugar and salt.
Fry the minced lemongrass with the chili flakes, garlic and annatto oil over low heat for 3 minutes, and stir half of this sate oil into the broth so it turns red-orange.
Put noodles in each bowl, top with sliced shank, a knuckle slice and cha Hue, ladle the boiling broth over, and serve with herbs, banana blossom, lime and the rest of the sate oil.

dishes.name: Com Hen (Hue Baby Clam Rice)

ingredients: 1 kg baby river clams (hen) from the Huong river (or small clams/cockles)
4 bowls cooked rice, cooled to room temperature
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1/2 tsp pepper
100 g pork cracklings (tep mo) and 3 tbsp roasted peanuts
3 tbsp toasted sesame and 4 rice crackers, crushed
1 handful shredded banana blossom, starfruit, Vietnamese mint, herbs
2 tbsp mam ruoc (shrimp paste) mixed with chili, and 1 tsp chili oil
steps: Soak the clams in salted water for 1 hour to purge sand, then boil them in 600 ml water for 5 minutes until they open; scoop out the meat and keep the clam broth hot.
Fry the shallot and garlic in oil, add the clam meat, fish sauce and pepper and stir-fry over high heat for 3-4 minutes until dry and fragrant.
Put cool rice in bowls and pile on the clams, herbs, banana blossom, starfruit, peanuts, sesame, cracklings and crushed crackers.
Add a little shrimp paste and chili oil, and serve with a small bowl of the hot clam broth to pour in or sip on the side.

dishes.name: Bun Hen (Hue Baby Clam Noodles)

ingredients: 1 kg baby river clams (hen) (or small clams/cockles)
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1/2 tsp pepper
100 g pork cracklings and 3 tbsp roasted peanuts
3 tbsp toasted sesame and 2 rice crackers, crushed
1 handful herbs, banana blossom and sliced starfruit
2 tbsp mam ruoc with chili, to taste
steps: Purge the clams in salted water for 1 hour, then boil in 600 ml water for 5 minutes until open; pick out the meat and keep the broth.
Stir-fry the clam meat with shallot, garlic, fish sauce and pepper over high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Put vermicelli in bowls, top with clams, herbs, banana blossom, starfruit, cracklings, peanuts, sesame and crackers.
Season with shrimp paste and chili, and pour over a ladle of the hot clam broth before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Khoai (Hue Crispy Pancake)

ingredients: 200 g rice flour and 1 tbsp glutinous rice flour
Tuong dip: 3 tbsp fermented soybean paste simmered with pork liver, sesame and peanuts (or hoisin with peanut butter)
To serve: lettuce, herbs, sliced starfruit and green banana
steps: Whisk the flours, water, egg, turmeric and salt into a thin batter and rest 20 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp lard in a small heavy pan (Hue uses a long-handled cast-iron pan) over high heat, fry a few slices of pork and shrimp for 1 minute until coloured.
Pour in a ladle of batter, swirl, add bean sprouts, cover for 1 minute, then uncover and fry 3-4 minutes more, adding lard round the edge, until deep golden and crisp; fold in half.
Serve hot with lettuce, herbs, starfruit and green banana, dipped in the tuong peanut-liver sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Beo (Steamed Rice Cakes with Shrimp)

ingredients: 200 g rice flour and 2 tbsp tapioca starch
150 g shrimp, peeled, boiled and pounded to floss (tom chay)
2 tbsp spring onion oil (spring onion warmed in 3 tbsp oil)
Nuoc cham: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp water, chili and garlic
steps: Whisk the flours, salt, oil and water and rest 1 hour.
Set small saucers or ramekins in a steamer and heat them for 2 minutes over high heat.
Fill each saucer with a thin layer of batter and steam for 6-7 minutes until set and translucent with a small dimple in the middle.
Dry-fry the pounded shrimp over low heat for 5 minutes until fluffy and orange.
Top each cake with spring onion oil, shrimp floss and cracklings, then spoon on nuoc cham and eat straight from the saucers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Nam (Flat Steamed Rice Dumplings)

ingredients: 200 g rice flour and 1 tbsp tapioca starch
2 shallots, minced, and 1 tbsp annatto oil
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1/2 tsp pepper
12 pieces banana leaf, 15 x 20 cm, wiped and oiled
Nuoc cham with chili, to serve
steps: Cook the rice flour, starch, salt and water in a pan over low heat, stirring constantly, for 5-6 minutes until it thickens into a smooth paste.
Fry the shallot in annatto oil, add the shrimp and pork, season with fish sauce and pepper and cook 5 minutes until dry and reddish.
Spread 2 tbsp batter thinly on each oiled leaf, scatter filling along the middle, and fold the leaf into a flat rectangular packet.
Steam over high heat for 15-20 minutes until the batter is translucent.
Serve in the leaf, with nuoc cham spooned over when unwrapped.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Bot Loc (Tapioca Shrimp and Pork Dumplings)

ingredients: 200 ml boiling water and 1/2 tsp salt
200 g small shrimp, shell on (Hue cooks keep the shell for crunch)
2 shallots, minced, and 1 tbsp annatto oil
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp pepper
12 pieces banana leaf (optional, for the leaf-wrapped version)
Nuoc cham with chili and spring onion oil, to serve
steps: Cook the shrimp and pork with shallot, annatto oil, fish sauce, sugar and pepper over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until caramelised and dry.
Pour the boiling water over the tapioca starch and salt, stir, then knead to a smooth, elastic dough.
Roll small balls, flatten each, place one shrimp and a piece of pork in the middle and fold into a half-moon (or spread on banana leaf and fold for the leaf version).
Boil the bare dumplings for 6-8 minutes until clear and floating, then drop into cold water; steam the leaf-wrapped ones for 20 minutes until translucent.
Drizzle with spring onion oil and serve with nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Ram It (Fried Sticky Rice Dumplings)

ingredients: 300 g glutinous rice flour, 230 ml warm water and 1/2 tsp salt
150 g shrimp, chopped, and 100 g minced pork
2 shallots, minced, and 1 tbsp annatto oil
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1/2 tsp pepper
50 g shrimp floss and spring onion oil, for topping
Nuoc cham with chili, to serve
steps: Knead the flour, salt and water into a soft dough; divide in two.
Fry the shallot in annatto oil, add shrimp and pork, season with fish sauce and pepper and cook 6 minutes until dry.
With half the dough, make flat discs about 5 cm wide and deep-fry at 170°C for 3-4 minutes until crisp and golden (the ram bases).
With the other half, fill small rounds with the meat mixture and pinch into dumplings (the it); steam over high heat for 10 minutes until translucent.
Set each sticky dumpling on a crisp fried disc, add spring onion oil and shrimp floss, and serve with nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Uot Thit Nuong (Hue Rice Sheets with Grilled Pork)

ingredients: 500 g fresh thin rice sheets (banh uot)
2 stalks lemongrass, 3 shallots and 3 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp honey
1 handful lettuce, mint, perilla and cucumber
Tuong dip: fermented soybean paste with peanuts and sesame (or hoisin and peanut butter)
steps: Marinate the pork with lemongrass, shallot, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, honey, oil and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Thread onto skewers or a grill basket and grill over hot charcoal for 3-4 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Lay a rice sheet flat, add lettuce, herbs, cucumber and several pieces of pork, and roll up.
Serve the rolls with the peanut tuong dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nem Lui (Lemongrass Pork Skewers)

ingredients: 500 g minced pork (with some fat), plus 50 g pork skin, boiled and finely chopped
3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp pepper
12 stalks lemongrass, trimmed to 20 cm skewers
1 packet rice paper, plus lettuce, herbs, cucumber, starfruit, green banana
Tuong dip with liver, peanuts and sesame (or hoisin and peanut butter)
steps: Pound or process the pork with garlic, shallot, fish sauce, sugar, pepper and baking powder until sticky, then mix in the pork skin and chill 30 minutes.
With oiled hands, wrap a sausage of the mixture around the upper half of each lemongrass stalk, pressing firmly.
Grill over medium charcoal for 12-15 minutes, turning and brushing with oil, until browned and cooked through.
Slide the pork off into soft rice paper with herbs and vegetables, roll and dip in the thick peanut tuong.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cha Tom Hue (Hue Shrimp Cake)

ingredients: 400 g raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
150 g pork fat, diced fine and blanched
2 egg yolks, plus 1 extra yolk for glazing
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp pepper
steps: Pound the shrimp to a sticky paste with the fish sauce, sugar, pepper and shallot, then mix in the pork fat and 2 yolks.
Spread the paste 2 cm thick in an oiled tray and brush with the extra yolk mixed with annatto oil.
Steam over high heat for 20 minutes until firm.
Grill or pan-fry the slab on both sides for 3-4 minutes until golden, then cut into strips and serve with rice, pickles and nuoc cham, a dish once served at the Hue court.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tre Hue (Fermented Pork in Guava Leaves)

ingredients: 500 g pork ears and pork skin, boiled until just tender
300 g lean pork, boiled and thinly sliced
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt
1 large bunch guava leaves (la oi), plus banana leaves and string
steps: Boil the pork ears, skin and lean meat in salted water for 20 minutes until fully cooked; cool and slice everything into thin julienne.
Mix the pork with galangal, garlic, chili, sesame, toasted rice powder, fish sauce, sugar and salt, working it well with clean gloves.
Line squares of banana leaf with guava leaves, add a portion of the mix, wrap tightly into balls or bricks and tie with string.
Leave at cool room temperature for 2-3 days until pleasantly sour (a traditional lactic ferment); keep clean and refrigerate once sour, eat within a week.
Unwrap and serve with fresh herbs, sliced green banana and a little chili fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tom Chua Hue (Hue Fermented Sour Shrimp)

ingredients: 500 g very fresh small shrimp, heads and legs trimmed
200 ml rice wine (ruou trang), for rinsing
steps: Soak the trimmed shrimp in the rice wine for 10 minutes (this softens the shells and cleans them), drain and pat completely dry.
Mix the shrimp with salt and sugar and rest 1 hour, then add galangal, garlic, chili, glutinous rice and fish sauce.
Pack into the sterilised jar pressing down firmly, close and keep at cool room temperature for 4-5 days until the shells turn red and the taste is sour; this is a traditional ferment.
Refrigerate once sour and eat within 2 weeks; serve with boiled pork belly, herbs, green banana and starfruit.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mam Ruoc Hue (Hue Fermented Shrimp Paste Dip)

ingredients: 3 tbsp mam ruoc Hue (Hue fermented krill paste), bought (or Thai kapi)
2 tbsp pineapple, finely chopped, or 1 tbsp lime juice
steps: Fry the garlic and chili in oil over low heat for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the mam ruoc, sugar and water and stir constantly for 3-4 minutes until smooth, thick and no longer raw-smelling.
Off the heat, stir in pineapple or lime juice.
Serve as the dip for boiled pork, green mango, young jackfruit salad and Hue rice dishes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Canh Nam Pho (Nam Pho Thick Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 300 g rice flour and 100 g tapioca starch, for the noodles
400 ml boiling water and 1/2 tsp salt
300 g shrimp, peeled (shells reserved), and 200 g crab meat
2 tbsp annatto oil and 3 shallots, minced
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt
1 tbsp tapioca starch, mixed with water
1 handful spring onion, coriander and pepper
steps: Simmer the pork bones and shrimp shells in 2 l water for 1 hour, then strain.
Mix rice flour, tapioca and salt with the boiling water into a soft dough, roll thinly and cut into thick strips.
Fry the shallots in annatto oil, add shrimp and crab, season with fish sauce, and cook 3 minutes until the shrimp turn pink.
Bring the broth to a boil, add the noodles and cook 5-6 minutes until translucent and the broth thickens; add the shrimp-crab mixture and thicken a little more with the starch water.
Season with sugar and salt and serve hot, orange-red and slightly gluey, topped with spring onion, coriander and pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Com Am Phu (Hue Hell Rice)

ingredients: 300 g pork shoulder, sliced, marinated with fish sauce, sugar and lemongrass
150 g Hue pork sausage (cha lua), julienned
2 eggs, beaten and fried into a thin omelette, julienned
1 cucumber, 1 carrot and 1 handful herbs, julienned
Nuoc cham: 4 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp water, lime, garlic and chili
steps: Grill the marinated pork over charcoal for 3-4 minutes per side until cooked and charred, then slice.
Stir-fry the shrimp in oil with a little fish sauce for 2-3 minutes until pink and cooked.
Arrange rice in the middle of each plate and surround it with rows of pork, shrimp, sausage, omelette, cucumber, carrot and herbs in a colourful ring.
Serve with nuoc cham to pour over; the name comes from a late-night eatery that served this by dim lamplight.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Com Sen (Lotus Leaf Rice)

ingredients: 400 g jasmine rice, cooked slightly dry
100 g fresh or dried lotus seeds (hat sen), cored and boiled until soft
150 g Chinese sausage (lap xuong) or chicken, diced
2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp fish sauce
2 large lotus leaves, soaked in hot water
steps: Stir-fry the sausage, shrimp, mushroom, carrot and peas in oil over high heat for 4-5 minutes until cooked.
Add the rice and lotus seeds, season with soy and fish sauce, and toss until hot and evenly coloured.
Divide onto the softened lotus leaves and fold into tight parcels, tying with string if needed.
Steam over high heat for 20-25 minutes so the rice absorbs the lotus fragrance.
Cut open the leaf at the table and serve, a dish of the Nguyen imperial kitchens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Ep Hue (Pressed Tapioca Cake)

ingredients: 200 g tapioca starch and 50 g rice flour
100 g minced pork and 100 g shrimp, chopped
2 eggs (optional, Hue often adds a quail egg)
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1/2 tsp pepper
To serve: herbs, pickled green papaya, nuoc cham with chili
steps: Mix the starches, salt and water into a smooth batter.
Fry the shallot in oil, add pork and shrimp with fish sauce and pepper, and cook 5 minutes.

On a hot lightly oiled griddle (or a sandwich press), pour a thin round of batter, add a spoon of filling (or an egg), and press down firmly with a flat lid for 2-3 minutes until crisp, thin and translucent.
Serve hot rolled around herbs and pickled papaya, dipped in nuoc cham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mit Tron (Hue Young Jackfruit Salad)

ingredients: 600 g young green jackfruit (mit non), peeled (or canned young jackfruit in brine)
200 g pork belly, boiled and thinly sliced
3 tbsp roasted sesame and 3 tbsp roasted peanuts
1 handful Vietnamese coriander and mint, chopped
2 tbsp mam ruoc Hue dip (or fish sauce), 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp lime juice
2 cloves garlic, 2 shallots and 2 chilies, minced
Toasted sesame rice crackers, to serve
steps: Boil the jackfruit in salted water for 30-40 minutes until tender, drain, cool and shred or slice thinly.
Fry the garlic and shallot in oil, add the jackfruit, pork and shrimp and toss for 3 minutes.
Season with mam ruoc, sugar, lime and chili, then mix in the herbs, peanuts and sesame.
Serve scooped onto broken sesame rice crackers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Va Tron (Hue Fig Salad)

ingredients: 500 g young green cluster figs (trai va), sliced thin (or green unripe figs or young jackfruit)
200 g pork belly, boiled and thinly sliced
1 tbsp lime juice in 1 l water, for soaking
2 tbsp mam ruoc Hue, 1 tbsp sugar and 2 chilies
steps: Soak the sliced figs in lime water for 10 minutes to stop browning, then boil for 3 minutes, drain and squeeze dry.
Fry the garlic in oil, add mam ruoc, sugar and chili and stir 2 minutes to make the dressing.
Toss the figs with pork, shrimp and dressing, then add herbs, sesame and peanuts.
Serve with sesame rice crackers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Bot Loc Heo Quay (Tapioca Pudding with Roast Pork)

ingredients: 200 g Chinese-style roast pork belly (heo quay), skin on, cut into small cubes
200 g rock sugar or white sugar
1 tbsp tapioca starch mixed with water (to thicken)
steps: Knead the tapioca starch with the boiling water into a smooth dough, then wrap each small cube of roast pork inside a marble-size ball.
Simmer the sugar and ginger in 1 l water until dissolved.
Drop the balls into a pot of boiling water and cook 8-10 minutes until clear and floating, then move them into the ginger syrup.
Thicken the syrup slightly with the starch water and simmer 2 minutes.
Serve warm in small bowls; the sweet-salty contrast is a famous Hue royal dessert.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Hat Sen Long Nhan (Lotus Seed and Longan Sweet Soup)

ingredients: 200 g fresh or dried Hue lotus seeds (hat sen), cored
24 fresh longans (long nhan), peeled and seeded (or canned longans)
steps: Soak dried lotus seeds for 2 hours (fresh need no soaking), then simmer them in the water with pandan for 30 minutes until soft but whole.
Add the rock sugar and simmer 5 minutes more until dissolved; let cool.
Wrap each lotus seed inside a longan.
Serve the stuffed longans in the cool syrup with crushed ice, an elegant imperial Hue dessert.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Dau Ngu (Lima Bean Sweet Soup)

ingredients: 200 g dried white lima beans (dau ngu)
150 g rock sugar or white sugar
steps: Soak the lima beans overnight, then peel off the skins.
Simmer the beans with ginger and pandan in the water over low heat for 45-50 minutes until tender but still whole.
Add the sugar and simmer 10 minutes more so the beans absorb the syrup.
Serve warm, or cool with crushed ice, as sold along the Hue streets.

dishes.name: Me Xung (Hue Sesame Peanut Candy)

ingredients: 200 g malt syrup (mach nha) or glucose syrup
100 g tapioca starch, cooked with 200 ml water to a clear paste
steps: Cook the malt syrup, sugar and ginger juice in a heavy pan over low heat for 10 minutes until bubbling.
Add the tapioca paste and stir constantly for 20-25 minutes until it becomes a thick, elastic, translucent mass that pulls away from the pan.
Mix in the peanuts, then pour onto an oiled tray thickly coated with sesame and press another layer of sesame on top.

dishes.name: Mi Quang (Quang Nam Turmeric Noodles)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 600 g fresh wide turmeric rice noodles (mi Quang) (or wide rice noodles tossed with 1/2 tsp turmeric oil)
300 g pork belly and 300 g shrimp, shell on
4 quail eggs, boiled and peeled (or 2 hen eggs)
1 tsp turmeric powder and 1 tbsp annatto oil

1 handful lettuce, banana blossom, mint, basil, rau ram, lime and chili
steps: Slice the pork, trim the shrimp, and marinate both with half the shallot and garlic, turmeric, fish sauce, sugar and pepper for 20 minutes.

dishes.name: Cao Lau (Hoi An Pork Noodles)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

500 g pork shoulder (for xa xiu-style char siu)
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp five-spice
100 g crisp fried noodle squares (or pork cracklings)
1 handful Tra Que herbs: lettuce, mint, basil, rau ram, bean sprouts
Lime and chili jam, to serve
steps: Marinate the pork with soy, fish sauce, sugar, five-spice, garlic and shallot for 1 hour.

dishes.name: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An Chicken Rice)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

2 shallots, minced, and 1 thumb ginger, sliced
1 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp fish sauce
1 onion, thinly sliced and soaked in vinegar-sugar water
1 handful rau ram (Vietnamese coriander), plus green papaya pickle
Chili jam (tuong ot) and lime, to serve
steps: Simmer the chicken with ginger and salt in water to cover for 30-35 minutes until the juices run clear, then plunge into cold water; reserve the stock.

dishes.name: Banh Mi Hoi An (Hoi An Style Banh Mi)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 200 g cha lua (Vietnamese pork sausage), sliced
200 g char siu-style roast pork, sliced
4 tbsp mayonnaise (butter and egg yolk style)
2 tbsp Hoi An chili jam (tuong ot) and 2 tbsp pork braising sauce
1 cucumber, sliced, and 1 handful pickled carrot and daikon

steps: Warm the baguettes in a hot oven or over charcoal for 3-4 minutes until the crust crackles.

dishes.name: Banh Bao Banh Vac (Hoi An White Rose Dumplings)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

250 ml boiling water and 1/2 tsp salt
200 g shrimp, pounded to a paste
1 shallot, minced, and 1 tbsp fish sauce
Nuoc cham: fish sauce, sugar, lime, water and chili
steps: Knead the rice flour, starch and salt with the boiling water into a smooth dough; rest 20 minutes covered.
Mix the shrimp, pork, shallot and fish sauce into a filling.
Roll small pieces of dough very thin into 6 cm rounds, place a little filling in the centre and pinch the edges up, leaving the top open and frilled like a rose.

dishes.name: Hoanh Thanh Chien (Hoi An Fried Wontons)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 200 g minced pork and 100 g shrimp, chopped
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1/2 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp pepper
Topping: 100 g shrimp, 100 g minced pork, 1 tomato, 1 onion, 2 tbsp pineapple, diced
2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp vinegar and 100 ml water
steps: Mix the pork, chopped shrimp, fish sauce, sugar and pepper and place a teaspoon on each wrapper, folding into triangles and sealing with water.

dishes.name: Che Bap (Sweet Corn Pudding)

200 ml coconut milk with a pinch of salt
steps: Simmer the corn cobs in the water for 15 minutes to flavour it, then remove them.

dishes.name: Banh Dap (Smashed Rice Cracker and Rice Sheet)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

4 freshly steamed wet rice sheets (banh uot), about 25 cm
150 g boiled pork or shrimp, sliced (optional topping)

Lay a hot wet rice sheet on top of each cracker and another cracker on top, then smash with your palm (dap means smash) to make crack-sound pieces.

Break into pieces and dip into the mam nem sauce, as served along the Thu Bon river in Hoi An.

dishes.name: Be Thui Cau Mong (Cau Mong Roasted Veal)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

Mam nem dip: 3 tbsp mam nem, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp pineapple, garlic and chili

steps: Rub the veal with salt and lemongrass and roast it over a hot straw or charcoal fire (thui), turning constantly, until the skin is golden-brown and crisp, about 40 minutes.

dishes.name: Banh Trang Cuon Thit Heo (Da Nang Pork Belly Rice Paper Rolls)

Mam nem dip: 3 tbsp mam nem, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp pineapple, garlic, chili and lime
steps: Simmer the pork with salt and shallot for 25-30 minutes until a skewer brings up clear juices, then plunge into cold water.

Soften a rice paper, layer herbs, vegetables and pork, then roll tightly.

dishes.name: Bun Mam Nem (Da Nang Anchovy Sauce Noodles)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 300 g pork belly, boiled and sliced
200 g nem chua (fermented pork roll) and 100 g cha bo (beef sausage), sliced

Mam nem sauce: 4 tbsp mam nem, 2 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp pineapple, 2 cloves garlic, 2 chilies, 1 tbsp lime juice, 3 tbsp water

dishes.name: Mam Nem (Fermented Anchovy Dip)

dishes.name: Goi Ca Nam O (Nam O Raw Fish Salad)

dishes.name: Bun Cha Ca (Fish Cake Noodle Soup)

dishes.name: Bun Sua (Nha Trang Jellyfish Noodle Soup)

steps: Soak the jellyfish in several changes of cold water for 30 minutes to remove the salt, then cut into strips.

Lettuce, herbs, cucumber, green mango, starfruit and pickled carrot
steps: Pound or process the pork with fish sauce, sugar, garlic, baking powder and pepper until very sticky, mix in the fat, and chill 30 minutes.

dishes.name: Banh Can (Mini Rice Pancakes)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

Green mango, cucumber and herbs, to serve
steps: Blend the soaked rice with water and salt until very smooth and rest 30 minutes.
Heat a clay banh can mould (or an aebleskiver pan) over high heat, lightly oil, and pour batter into each hole.

dishes.name: Banh Xeo Tom Nhay (Binh Dinh Jumping Shrimp Pancakes)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

300 g very fresh small shrimp (tom nhay), shell on
Lettuce, herbs, rice paper, and nuoc cham or a peanut-liver dip

dishes.name: Banh Hoi Chao Long (Binh Dinh Rice Vermicelli Mats with Offal Congee)

ingredients: 500 g banh hoi (fine rice vermicelli mats)

2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper

dishes.name: Nem Cho Huyen (Binh Dinh Fermented Pork)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 500 g very fresh lean pork leg, minced finely
150 g pork skin, boiled 15 minutes and julienned
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt
4 cloves garlic, sliced, and 4 chilies, sliced
1 bunch guava leaves or chum ruot leaves
steps: Pound the very fresh pork with fish sauce, sugar and salt until sticky, then mix in the pork skin and peppercorns.

dishes.name: Banh It La Gai (Binh Dinh Ramie Leaf Dumplings)

dishes.name: Ca Bong Song Tra Kho (Braised Tra River Gobies)

ingredients: 500 g ca bong (small river gobies from the Tra Khuc river) (or other small freshwater fish)

dishes.name: Don Quang Ngai (Quang Ngai Baby Clam Soup)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 1 kg don (tiny Quang Ngai river mussels) (or baby clams)
1 tbsp fish sauce and 1/2 tsp salt
1 handful spring onion and rau ram, chopped
steps: Soak the don in water for 1 hour, then boil in 1.5 l water for 5 minutes until open; strain the broth through a cloth and pick out the meat.

dishes.name: Goi Ca Mai (Phan Thiet Raw Herring Salad)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 500 g very fresh sashimi-grade ca mai (round herring/sprat), filleted (use only sushi-grade, previously frozen fish)
2 tbsp roasted peanuts and 2 tbsp toasted rice powder
1 shallot, sliced, and 1 thumb galangal, julienned
1 handful herbs: perilla, mint, wild betel and green banana slices

steps: Use only sashimi-grade fish, kept ice-cold; soak the fillets in lime juice for 10 minutes until opaque white, then squeeze dry.

Roll the fish with herbs and green banana in rice paper and dip into the peanut sauce.

dishes.name: Lau Tha Phan Thiet (Phan Thiet Fish Salad Hot Pot)
dishes.cuisine: Central Coast (Quang Nam, Da Nang & South Central)

ingredients: 400 g mackerel or snapper fillet, half cut into slices, half grilled and flaked
200 g squid and 200 g shrimp, cleaned
100 g pork belly, boiled and sliced
1 kg fish bones and 2 tomatoes, for the broth
1 tbsp tamarind paste, 2 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tsp sugar
1 green papaya and 1 cucumber, julienned, plus pickled onion
3 tbsp roasted peanuts, sesame crackers and fried shallots
500 g rice vermicelli, herbs and lime
steps: Soak the raw fish slices in lime juice for 10 minutes; boil the squid and shrimp for 2-3 minutes until cooked, then slice.

Simmer the fish bones, tomatoes and tamarind in 1.5 l water for 30 minutes, strain and season with fish sauce and sugar to make a sour broth; keep it boiling on a table burner.

dishes.name: Pho Kho Gia Lai (Gia Lai Two-bowl Pho)

ingredients: 1.5 kg pork and beef bones, blanched
400 g dried thin rice noodles (banh pho kho Gia Lai), soaked 20 minutes
2 tbsp black soy sauce and 1 tbsp oyster sauce
2 tbsp shallot oil with fried shallots
1 handful bean sprouts, Thai basil and chopped scallions
chilli sauce and lime wedges, to serve
steps: Simmer the blanched bones with the charred onion and ginger in 3 litres water on low heat for 2.5 hours, skimming often, then season with 2 tbsp fish sauce.

Mix the black soy sauce, oyster sauce and shallot oil into a glossy dressing.
Blanch the noodles in boiling water for 20 seconds, drain well and toss each portion with 1 tbsp of the dressing.
Serve the noodles in one bowl topped with minced pork, fried shallots and scallions, and a second small bowl of boiling broth poured over the raw beef slices so they turn pink.
Eat the dry noodles with herbs, sprouts, chilli sauce and lime, sipping the broth alongside.

dishes.name: Bo Mot Nang Gia Lai (Sun-dried Beef)

ingredients: 800 g beef topside, cut along the grain into 3 cm strips
1 tsp salt and 1 tsp ground black pepper
muoi kien vang (golden ant salt) or chilli salt, to serve
steps: Rub the beef with lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, salt, pepper and chilli, then marinate in the fridge for 2 hours.
Dry the strips on racks in hot sun for one day, or in a 60 C oven with the door ajar for 6–8 hours, until the outside is firm and the inside still slightly supple.

dishes.name: Muoi Kien Vang (Golden Ant Salt)

ingredients: 100 g golden weaver ants and their eggs (kien vang), cleaned
steps: Dry-roast the ants in a pan over low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until fragrant, crisp and cooked through.

Pound the lemongrass, chillies and garlic in a mortar to a coarse paste, then add the roasted salt, sugar and ants and pound until evenly mixed and orange.

dishes.name: Goi La Kon Tum (Kon Tum Leaf Salad)

150 g fermented rice (com me) or fermented soybean paste

steps: Boil the pork belly in salted water for 25 minutes until cooked through, cool and slice thin; boil the prawns for 2–3 minutes until pink, peel and halve.

dishes.name: Ga Nuong Ban Don (Ban Don Grilled Chicken)

ingredients: 1 tbsp mac khen (wild prickly ash pepper) or Sichuan pepper, crushed
golden ant salt or salt-pepper-lime dip, to serve
steps: Pound lemongrass, mac khen, garlic and shallots, mix with honey, fish sauce, salt and oil and rub all over the chicken; marinate 1 hour.

Check that the thigh juices run clear and the skin is golden and crisp.
Chop into pieces and serve with sticky rice in bamboo, wild herbs and ant salt or salt-pepper-lime dip.

dishes.name: Canh Thut (Ede Bamboo Tube Soup)

ingredients: 300 g pork ribs or chicken, chopped small
200 g pumpkin leaves and bitter vegetables, torn
100 g fresh bamboo shoot, boiled and sliced
steps: Season the meat with salt, chilli and lemongrass and pack it with the eggplant and bamboo shoot into a fresh bamboo tube (or a heavy pot), adding 600 ml water.
Stand the tube in a wood fire or simmer the pot on low heat for 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the leaves, then stir in the ground rice and churn with a stick or spoon for 10 minutes until thick and porridge-like.
Taste for salt and serve with rice and dried beef.

dishes.name: Bun Do Buon Ma Thuot (Buon Ma Thuot Red Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 300 g pork paste (gio song) and 150 g fish cake, sliced
200 g crab paste or minced crab and pork
3 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp sugar
banana blossom, lettuce, mint and chilli sate, to serve
steps: Simmer the pork bones in 3 litres water on low for 1 hour, skimming, then strain.
Fry the shallots in annatto oil until fragrant, add tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until soft, then pour in the broth with fish sauce and sugar.
Shape the crab-pork mix and pork paste into spoonfuls and drop them into the simmering broth for 6–8 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Put vermicelli and fish cake in bowls, ladle over the red broth and meatballs, and serve with shredded banana blossom, herbs and chilli sate.

dishes.name: Banh Uot Long Ga (Rice Sheets with Chicken and Giblets)

ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 1.2 kg) plus 200 g giblets and unlaid eggs if available
1 onion, thinly sliced and soaked in vinegar
3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp lime juice
1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp ground pepper
steps: Poach the chicken in salted water at a gentle simmer for 30 minutes, adding the giblets for the last 10 minutes, until the juices run clear; plunge in ice water.
Shred the meat and slice the giblets; toss with rau ram, pickled onion, salt and pepper.
Mix fish sauce, sugar, lime, garlic, chilli and 6 tbsp water into a dipping sauce.
Steam the rice sheets for 1 minute to warm, sprinkle with fried shallots and serve with the chicken salad, a bowl of chicken broth and the sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Phe Phin Buon Ma Thuot (Robusta Phin Coffee)

ingredients: 25 g dark-roast Buon Ma Thuot robusta coffee, medium-coarse ground
steps: Put condensed milk in a glass if using, set the phin filter on top, add the coffee and level it, then press the inner screen gently.
Pour in 20 ml hot water, wait 30 seconds for the grounds to bloom, then fill the phin and cover.
Let it drip slowly for 4–5 minutes; if it drips too fast, press the screen tighter next time.
Stir and drink hot, or pour over ice for ca phe sua da.

dishes.name: Ruou Can (Rice Wine Drunk through Bamboo Straws)

ingredients: 1 jar ruou can (Central Highlands rice-and-leaf jar wine) from a licensed producer
grilled meats and sun-dried beef, to serve
steps: Ruou can is a fermented rice wine made by Ede, M'nong, Ba Na and other highland peoples, sealed in earthen jars with rice husks and forest leaves; buy a sealed jar from a licensed producer rather than making it at home.
To serve, open the jar, remove the leaf seal and top up with cool water to just below the rim, then push in the bamboo straws.
Guests sip in turns around the jar during festivals, with a small marker floating on the surface showing each person's share, and the jar is refilled with water as it goes down.
Serve with grilled chicken, sun-dried beef and ant salt, and drink in moderation.

dishes.name: Banh Trang Nuong (Da Lat Grilled Rice Paper)

ingredients: 4 quail eggs or 2 chicken eggs, beaten
100 g minced pork or dried shrimp
4 scallions, chopped and wilted in 2 tbsp hot oil (mo hanh)
mayonnaise and chilli sauce, to serve
steps: Lay a rice paper on a rack over low charcoal or in a dry pan over low heat.
Spread a little beaten egg over it with a spoon, then scatter pork, sausage, scallion oil and shrimp floss.
Grill for 3–4 minutes, moving it often, until the egg and pork are fully cooked and the paper is crisp and blistered.
Squiggle with mayonnaise and chilli sauce, fold in half and eat hot.
