dishes.name: Banh Mi Xiu Mai (Da Lat Meatball Banh Mi)

ingredients: 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp pepper
1 tbsp tomato paste and 1 tbsp annatto oil
chopped scallions and chilli sauce, to serve
steps: Mix the pork, jicama, half the garlic and shallots, fish sauce, sugar, pepper and starch, and roll into 4 cm balls.
Steam the balls for 15 minutes until firm.
Fry the remaining garlic and shallot in annatto oil, add tomatoes and paste and cook 5 minutes, then add stock and the meatballs and simmer 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve the meatballs in small bowls of sauce topped with scallions, with crisp bread for dipping and chilli sauce on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau Ga La E (Chicken Hot Pot with E Leaves)

ingredients: 2 large bunches la e (hairy basil leaves); substitute Thai basil with a few lemon basil leaves
1.5 kg chicken bones or 2 litres chicken stock
200 g bamboo shoots, boiled and sliced
3 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tsp salt
salt-pepper-lime dip with chopped la e, to serve
steps: Season the chicken with fish sauce, salt and a little pounded la e and lemongrass for 20 minutes.
Bring the stock to the boil with shallots and lemongrass, add bamboo shoots and chicken and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Bring the pot to the table on a burner and add mushrooms and handfuls of la e, letting them wilt for 30 seconds.
Serve with vermicelli and the salt-pepper-lime dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Atiso Ham Gio Heo (Artichoke and Pork Hock Soup)

ingredients: 1 pork hock (about 1 kg), chopped and blanched
2 scallions and a few coriander sprigs
steps: Simmer the blanched hock in 2.5 litres water with the onion on low heat for 1 hour, skimming.
Trim the tough outer leaves of the artichokes, cut into quarters, scrape out the choke and rub with lemon or soak in salt water.
Add the artichokes and carrots and simmer 40–50 minutes until the hock is tender and the artichoke hearts are soft.
Season with fish sauce, salt and sugar, top with scallions and coriander and serve with rice.

dishes.name: Tra Atiso (Artichoke Tea)

ingredients: 1 fresh artichoke, roots and stems or 20 g dried Da Lat artichoke tea
steps: Rinse the artichoke parts, cut into pieces and put in a pot with the water and pandan.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until the liquid turns dark amber; if using dried tea, steep 5 minutes in just-boiled water instead.
Strain, sweeten with rock sugar or honey and serve hot or over ice.

dishes.name: Kem Bo (Da Lat Avocado Ice Cream)

steps: Scoop the avocado flesh and mash or blend with the condensed milk and milk until smooth but thick.
Divide between glasses and chill for 10 minutes.
Top each with a scoop of coconut ice cream and toasted coconut and eat immediately.

dishes.name: Com Tam Suon Bi Cha (Broken Rice with Grilled Pork Chop)

ingredients: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp honey, 2 stalks lemongrass and 3 cloves garlic, minced
150 g shredded pork skin (bi) mixed with 2 tbsp toasted rice powder
200 g minced pork, 2 eggs, 20 g glass noodles and 10 g wood ear for cha trung (steamed egg meatloaf)
pickled carrot and daikon, sliced cucumber and tomato
nuoc mam pha (fish sauce, sugar, lime, garlic, chilli, water), to serve
steps: Wash the broken rice and cook with a little less water than usual in a rice cooker until fluffy.
Marinate the chops in fish sauce, sugar, honey, lemongrass and garlic for 1 hour, then grill over hot charcoal for 4–5 minutes per side until caramelised and cooked through.
Mix the minced pork with 1 egg, soaked noodles and wood ear, press into a bowl, steam 20 minutes, then brush with the remaining yolk and steam 3 minutes more to set the golden top.
Plate rice with a pork chop, a wedge of cha, a spoonful of bi, scallion oil, pickles and vegetables, and serve with sweet-sour fish sauce poured over.

dishes.name: Banh Mi Thit (Saigon Banh Mi)

ingredients: 100 g chicken or pork liver pate
200 g cha lua (Vietnamese pork roll), sliced
150 g thit nguoi (cold cut roast pork or head cheese), sliced
100 g pickled carrot and daikon (do chua)
coriander sprigs and sliced bird's-eye chilli
steps: Split the warm baguettes lengthwise without cutting through.
Spread one side with pate and the other with mayonnaise.
Layer in the cha lua and cold cuts, then the pickles, cucumber, coriander and chilli.
Sprinkle with Maggi seasoning, close and eat at once while the crust is crisp.

dishes.name: Banh Mi Chao (Sizzling Pan Banh Mi Breakfast)

ingredients: 100 g Chinese sausage (lap xuong) or meatballs, sliced
pickles, cucumber, tomato and Maggi seasoning
steps: Heat two small cast-iron pans (chao) over high heat until very hot and add the butter.
Add the sausage, cha lua and pate and fry for 1 minute, then crack in two eggs per pan.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and lacy at the edges and the yolks are still runny.
Serve still sizzling with baguettes for dipping, pickles, vegetables and Maggi.

dishes.name: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 50 g dried squid, toasted, and 30 g dried shrimp
400 g dried hu tieu (clear tapioca-rice noodles)
200 g minced pork and 200 g pork liver, sliced
3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp rock sugar
garlic chives, celery leaves, bean sprouts and fried garlic
steps: Simmer the blanched bones with dried squid, dried shrimp and daikon in 3.5 litres water on low heat for 1.5–2 hours, then season with fish sauce and rock sugar.
Poach the prawns, liver and minced pork (in small clumps) in the simmering broth for 2–3 minutes until just cooked.
Blanch the noodles for 15 seconds and drain.

Top bowls of noodles with the pork, liver, prawns and quail eggs, ladle over the hot broth and finish with chives, celery and fried garlic; serve with lime and chilli, or serve the broth on the side for the dry (kho) version.

dishes.name: Mi Vit Tiem (Braised Duck Egg Noodles)

ingredients: 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp dark soy
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 tsp five-spice
steps: Rub the duck with five-spice and soy, then fry skin-side down in oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until deep brown.
Put the duck, mushrooms, oyster sauce, sugars, spices and stock in a pot and braise covered on low heat for 1 hour until the meat is tender.
Blanch the noodles and bok choy separately in boiling water for 1 minute each.
Serve noodles in bowls with a duck leg, mushrooms and bok choy and ladle over the rich braising broth.

dishes.name: Banh Canh Cua (Crab Tapioca Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 2 mud crabs (about 1 kg), steamed, meat picked
500 g fresh banh canh (thick tapioca noodles); substitute udon
200 g prawns and 150 g crab-shaped fish cake
2 tbsp annatto oil and 3 shallots, minced
2 tbsp tapioca starch mixed with 4 tbsp water
steps: Simmer the pork bones in 2.5 litres water for 1 hour and strain.
Fry the shallots in annatto oil, add the crab meat and 1 tbsp fish sauce and stir-fry 2 minutes until fragrant.
Bring the broth back to the boil, add the noodles, prawns and fish cake and cook 4 minutes, then season with fish sauce and sugar and stir in the starch slurry to make a silky, slightly thick broth.
Ladle into bowls, top with the crab meat, quail eggs, scallions and pepper and serve with lime and chilli.

dishes.name: Banh Canh Trang Bang (Trang Bang Thick Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 1.5 kg pork bones and 1 pork hock
500 g fresh tapioca-rice banh canh noodles
3 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp sugar
1 large tray of herbs and leaves: mint, perilla, sliced young leaves, bean sprouts
steps: Simmer the blanched bones, hock and squid in 3 litres water on low heat for 1.5–2 hours until the hock is tender, then season with fish sauce, sugar and salt.
Remove the hock, slice it and keep warm.
Blanch the noodles in boiling water for 1–2 minutes until soft and chewy.
Serve noodles topped with sliced hock and shallot oil, ladle over clear broth, and eat with the tray of Tay Ninh herbs and the sweet-sour fish sauce.

dishes.name: Banh Trang Phoi Suong (Trang Bang Dew-dried Rice Paper Rolls)

ingredients: 20 sheets banh trang phoi suong (dew-dried Trang Bang rice paper); substitute thin rice paper softened in water
1 large bunch mixed herbs and wild leaves: mint, perilla, Vietnamese balm, young mango leaves
1 cucumber, sliced, and 1 handful bean sprouts
4 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp lime juice, garlic and chilli for nuoc mam me
steps: Boil the pork in salted water for 30–35 minutes until cooked through and tender, then slice thin.
Make the dipping sauce by stirring fish sauce, sugar, lime, garlic, chilli and 4 tbsp water until the sugar dissolves.
Lay a sheet of the soft rice paper flat, add herbs, vermicelli, cucumber and 2–3 slices of pork and roll up.
Dip each roll in the sauce and eat immediately.

dishes.name: Goi Cuon (Fresh Spring Rolls)

ingredients: 1 lettuce, mint, Thai basil and garlic chives
4 tbsp hoisin sauce, 2 tbsp peanut butter, 100 ml water
2 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts and chilli paste
steps: Boil the pork in salted water for 25 minutes until cooked through and slice thin; boil the prawns for 2 minutes until pink, peel and halve lengthwise.
Dip a rice paper in warm water for 2 seconds and lay it flat.
Place 3 prawn halves cut-side up in the centre, then pork, lettuce, herbs and vermicelli, fold in the sides and roll tightly with a chive stalk poking out.
Simmer hoisin, peanut butter and water for 2 minutes, top with peanuts and chilli and serve as the dip.

dishes.name: Bi Cuon (Shredded Pork Skin Rolls)

ingredients: 200 g pork skin, boiled and finely shredded
200 g lean pork, boiled and shredded
1 tbsp fried garlic and 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt
nuoc mam pha or peanut-hoisin sauce, to serve
steps: Boil the pork skin for 20 minutes and the lean pork for 25 minutes until cooked, cool and cut both into fine threads.
Toss with rice powder, fried garlic, sugar and salt until each strand is coated.
Wet a rice paper, add lettuce, herbs, vermicelli and a line of bi, then roll tightly with a chive stalk.
Serve with sweet-sour fish sauce or peanut-hoisin dip.

dishes.name: Bo Bia (Jicama and Sausage Rolls)

ingredients: 300 g jicama (cu san) and 1 carrot, julienned
3 tbsp hoisin, 1 tbsp peanut butter and crushed peanuts
steps: Stir-fry the jicama and carrot in oil for 5 minutes until tender, season with salt and cool.
Fry the sausage slices 2 minutes; beat the eggs and cook into a thin omelette, then slice into strips.
Wet a rice paper, add lettuce, basil, jicama, egg, sausage and dried shrimp and roll tightly.
Serve with hoisin-peanut sauce topped with crushed peanuts and chilli.

dishes.name: Cha Gio (Southern Fried Spring Rolls)

ingredients: 1 taro (200 g) and 1 carrot, finely grated
30 g glass noodles and 10 g wood ear mushroom, soaked and chopped
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp pepper
30 sheets small rice paper (or banh trang re lace paper)
lettuce, herbs and nuoc mam pha, to serve
steps: Mix the pork, prawns, taro, carrot, noodles, wood ear, egg and seasonings well.
Lightly wet each rice paper, spoon in a line of filling and roll tightly into finger-thick logs.
Fry in 170 C oil for 8–10 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp and the filling is cooked through; drain on a rack.
Wrap in lettuce with herbs and dip in sweet-sour fish sauce.

dishes.name: Bun Thit Nuong (Grilled Pork Vermicelli Bowl)

ingredients: 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp honey
2 stalks lemongrass, 3 shallots, 3 cloves garlic, minced
4 cha gio (fried spring rolls), cut in pieces
lettuce, mint, perilla, bean sprouts and cucumber
pickled carrot and daikon, crushed peanuts, scallion oil
steps: Marinate the pork in fish sauce, sugar, honey, lemongrass, shallot and garlic for at least 1 hour.
Grill over hot charcoal or under a grill for 3–4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Fill bowls with greens, herbs and vermicelli, then add the grilled pork and cha gio.
Top with pickles, peanuts and scallion oil and pour over plenty of sweet-sour fish sauce before tossing.

dishes.name: Banh Xeo (Sizzling Turmeric Crepes)

ingredients: 400 ml coconut milk and 200 ml water
200 g bean sprouts and 50 g soaked mung beans
mustard greens, lettuce, herbs and nuoc mam pha, to serve
steps: Whisk the flour, turmeric, coconut milk, water, scallions and a pinch of salt and rest the batter 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a little oil in a wok or 25 cm pan over high heat, add some pork and prawns and stir-fry 1–2 minutes until nearly cooked.
Pour in a ladle of batter and swirl to coat thinly, scatter sprouts and mung beans, cover for 2 minutes, then uncover and cook 4–5 minutes on medium until the edges are lacy and crisp.
Fold in half, slide out and repeat; eat by wrapping pieces in mustard greens with herbs and dipping in fish sauce.

dishes.name: Banh Khot (Vung Tau Mini Crispy Pancakes)

ingredients: 200 g rice flour and 1 tbsp cooked rice, blended
300 ml coconut milk and 150 ml water
mustard greens, lettuce, herbs and pickled papaya, with nuoc mam pha
steps: Blend the flour, rice, turmeric, coconut milk, water and a pinch of salt and rest 1 hour, then stir in the scallions.
Heat a banh khot (or aebleskiver) pan over medium-high heat with 1 tsp oil in each well until smoking.
Fill each well two-thirds with batter, place a prawn on top, cover and cook 4–5 minutes until the bottoms are crisp and golden and the prawns are pink.
Lift out, sprinkle with shrimp floss, and eat wrapped in greens with herbs, pickles and fish sauce.

dishes.name: Bo Kho (Vietnamese Beef Stew)

ingredients: 1 kg beef shank or brisket, cut in 4 cm cubes
1 tbsp bo kho spice mix (or five-spice with paprika)
2 tbsp annatto oil and 1 tbsp tomato paste
Thai basil, baguettes or rice noodles, to serve
steps: Marinate the beef with the spice mix, fish sauce, sugar and minced lemongrass for 1 hour.
Brown the beef in annatto oil over high heat for 6 minutes, then add tomato paste and stir 1 minute.
Add coconut water, 500 ml water, lemongrass, star anise and cinnamon and simmer covered on low heat for 2 hours until tender.
Add the carrots for the last 25 minutes until soft, then serve with Thai basil, lime, salt-pepper dip and crisp baguette.

dishes.name: Ca Ri Ga (Vietnamese Chicken Curry)

ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs on the bone, chopped
3 tbsp Vietnamese curry powder (bot ca ri, Ca Ri An Do type)
2 sweet potatoes, cut in chunks and fried until golden
400 ml coconut milk and 400 ml chicken stock
baguette or rice vermicelli, to serve
steps: Marinate the chicken in half the curry powder, fish sauce and sugar for 20 minutes.
Fry the shallots, garlic, lemongrass and remaining curry powder in oil for 2 minutes, then add the chicken and brown 6 minutes.
Add stock and simmer covered 20 minutes, then add coconut milk and sweet potatoes and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the potatoes tender.
Serve with baguette or vermicelli and a salt-pepper-lime dip.

dishes.name: Bo Luc Lac (Shaking Beef)

ingredients: 600 g beef sirloin or fillet, cut in 2.5 cm cubes
2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp black pepper
1 red and 1 green bell pepper, cubed
2 tbsp vegetable oil and 1 tbsp butter
watercress, tomato and salt-pepper-lime dip, to serve
steps: Marinate the beef with oyster sauce, soy, sugar, pepper and half the garlic for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok until smoking, add the beef in one layer, sear 1 minute without moving, then shake the pan for another 1–2 minutes until browned outside and medium inside.
Add butter, remaining garlic, onion and peppers and toss 1 minute more.
Pile onto watercress and tomato and serve with rice and the salt-pepper-lime dip.

dishes.name: Bo La Lot (Beef Wrapped in Betel Leaves)

ingredients: 500 g minced beef with a little pork fat
40 la lot (wild betel leaves); substitute grape leaves
2 stalks lemongrass, 3 shallots and 2 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp curry powder
2 tbsp scallion oil and crushed peanuts
rice vermicelli, herbs and mam nem or nuoc mam pha, to serve
steps: Mix the beef with lemongrass, shallots, garlic, fish sauce, sugar and curry powder and marinate 20 minutes.
Place a spoonful at the stem end of each leaf, shiny side out, and roll into a small cigar.
Grill over charcoal or pan-fry with a little oil for 6–8 minutes, turning, until the leaves are fragrant and the beef is cooked through.
Top with scallion oil and peanuts and eat with vermicelli, herbs and anchovy dip (mam nem) or fish sauce.

dishes.name: Bo Bit Tet (Vietnamese Pan Beefsteak)

ingredients: 2 beef steaks (sirloin or tenderloin, 150 g each), pounded thin
1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp soy sauce, 1 tsp pepper
fries, pate and baguettes, to serve
steps: Marinate the steaks with oyster sauce, soy, garlic and pepper for 30 minutes.
Heat a cast-iron sizzling plate until very hot, add butter and onion, then lay the steak on and sear 1–2 minutes per side to your liking.
Crack the eggs beside the steak and cook 2 minutes until the whites set.
Serve on the sizzling plate with tomato, fries, pate and baguettes to mop up the juices.

dishes.name: Bo Nhung Giam (Beef Fondue in Vinegar)

ingredients: 500 ml coconut water and 4 tbsp rice vinegar
20 sheets rice paper and 200 g rice vermicelli
lettuce, herbs, cucumber, pineapple and green banana slices
mam nem (pineapple anchovy dip), to serve
steps: Simmer the coconut water, vinegar, lemongrass, onion, shallots, sugar and salt in a table pot for 10 minutes until fragrant and tangy.
Bring the pot to the table on a burner and keep it boiling.
Dip a few beef slices into the boiling broth for 15–30 seconds until no longer pink.
Roll the beef in rice paper with greens, herbs, fruit and vermicelli and dip in mam nem.

dishes.name: Chim Cut Roti (Roasted Quail)

ingredients: 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey
salt-pepper-lime dip and herbs, to serve
steps: Marinate the quails with oyster sauce, soy, honey, five-spice, garlic and shallots for 1 hour.
Fry in hot oil over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes per side until golden.
Add the marinade and coconut water and simmer uncovered for 10–12 minutes, turning, until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze and the quail is cooked through.
Serve with salt-pepper-lime dip, cucumber and herbs, with beer or rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Com Ga Xoi Mo (Crispy Chicken Rice)

ingredients: 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp turmeric
500 ml chicken stock and 1 tbsp butter
1 tsp turmeric or tomato paste for colour
shredded green papaya pickle and chilli-garlic fish sauce
steps: Poach the chicken legs in salted water for 15 minutes, drain, pat dry and rub with fish sauce, salt, sugar and turmeric, then dry 30 minutes.
Cook the rice with stock, butter and colouring until fluffy, then stir-fry briefly in a pan until each grain separates.
Heat oil to 170 C and repeatedly ladle it over the legs (xoi mo) or deep-fry for 8–10 minutes until the skin is very crisp and the meat is cooked through.
Serve the chicken on the rice with papaya pickle and chilli fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pha Lau (Five-spice Braised Offal)

ingredients: 1 kg mixed pork or beef offal (intestines, stomach, lung, ear), well cleaned
3 tbsp salt and 3 tbsp vinegar for cleaning
1 tbsp five-spice powder and 2 star anise
baguette, sour-chilli dip and Vietnamese coriander
steps: Scrub the offal with salt and vinegar, rinse, then blanch in boiling water with ginger for 5 minutes and drain.
Marinate with five-spice, garlic, shallots, fish sauce and sugar for 20 minutes.
Fry in annatto oil for 5 minutes, add coconut water, star anise and water to cover and simmer on low for 1.5–2 hours until tender.
Serve in bowls with the broth, baguette for dipping and a salt-chilli-lime sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sup Cua (Saigon Crab Soup)

ingredients: 3 tbsp tapioca starch mixed with 6 tbsp water
1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, pepper
steps: Bring the stock to the boil with the fish sauce and sugar.
Add the crab meat, chicken and wood ear and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the starch slurry until the soup thickens, then drizzle in the beaten egg while stirring slowly to make ribbons.
Add the quail eggs, top with coriander, scallions and lots of pepper and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Xoi Man (Savory Sticky Rice)

ingredients: 100 g shredded pork char siu or braised pork
3 tbsp fried shallots and 2 tbsp scallion oil
steps: Drain the rice, toss with salt and steam for 30 minutes, then sprinkle with water and steam 10 minutes more until soft and sticky.
Fry the sausage slices for 3 minutes until crisp at the edges; warm the char siu with the soy sauce.
Scoop the sticky rice into bowls and top with sausage, char siu, quail eggs, pork floss, scallion oil and fried shallots.
Serve warm with a little chilli sauce for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bot Chien (Fried Rice Flour Cake with Egg)

ingredients: 300 g rice flour and 50 g tapioca starch
1 green papaya, shredded and pickled in vinegar and sugar
3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar and chilli sauce
steps: Cook the flours, water and salt in a pan on low heat, stirring, for 10 minutes into a thick dough, press into a tray, steam 30 minutes and cool until firm.
Cut the cake into 2 cm cubes and fry in oil over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Pour in beaten egg, swirl and cook 2 minutes, flip in sections and cook until set.
Top with scallions and pickled papaya and serve with sweet soy-vinegar sauce and chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Trang Tron (Rice Paper Salad)

ingredients: 100 g rice paper, cut in strips
2 tbsp dried shrimp and 50 g dried beef jerky, shredded
2 tbsp scallion oil and 1 tbsp chilli satay oil
1 tbsp lime or kumquat juice and 1 tbsp sugar
2 tbsp roasted peanuts and Vietnamese coriander (rau ram)
steps: Put the rice paper strips in a bowl and moisten with the lime juice and scallion oil.
Add the dried shrimp, beef jerky, green mango, sugar and chilli satay oil and toss well with gloved hands.
Fold in the quail eggs, peanuts, rau ram and fried shallots and eat at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Goi Du Du Kho Bo (Green Papaya Salad with Beef Jerky)

ingredients: 50 g beef liver jerky or extra jerky
1 handful Thai basil and Vietnamese coriander
3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp lime juice
steps: Soak the papaya in salted ice water for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Mix fish sauce, sugar, lime, garlic, chilli and 3 tbsp water into a dressing.
Pile papaya on plates, top with jerky, herbs and peanuts, and drizzle with dressing and sweet soy just before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Oc Len Xao Dua (Mud Creeper Snails in Coconut Milk)

ingredients: 1 kg oc len (mud creeper snails), soaked in rice water 2 hours
steps: Scrub the snails and cut off the tip of each shell so they can be sucked out.
Fry the garlic, lemongrass and chilli in oil until fragrant, then add the snails and toss 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk with fish sauce and sugar and simmer 10–12 minutes until the snails are cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Stir in rau ram and serve with toothpicks and the coconut sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Oc Huong Rang Muoi (Salt-roasted Babylon Snails)

ingredients: 1 kg oc huong (spotted Babylon snails), soaked in salted water
steps: Boil the snails for 5 minutes until cooked and drain well.
Fry the garlic in butter until golden, add the snails and toss over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add salt, chilli salt and sugar and stir-roast for 4–5 minutes until the shells are coated and the salt sticks.
Toss with rau ram and serve with a kumquat-salt-pepper dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Hot Vit Lon Xao Me (Tamarind Balut)

ingredients: 8 balut (fertilised duck eggs, hot vit lon)
3 tbsp tamarind pulp dissolved in 100 ml warm water
3 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp fish sauce
steps: Boil the balut for 20 minutes until fully cooked, then peel.
Strain the tamarind, then simmer with sugar and fish sauce for 5 minutes until syrupy.
Fry the garlic in butter, add the balut and tamarind sauce and toss gently for 2 minutes until glossy.
Top with peanuts, rau ram and chilli and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bap Xao (Saigon Stir-fried Corn)

ingredients: 4 ears sweet corn, kernels cut off
steps: Melt the butter in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the dried shrimp for 1 minute.
Add the corn, sugar and salt and stir-fry for 5 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Add the scallions and toss 30 seconds, then serve in cups with chilli sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Tet (Cylindrical Sticky Rice Cake)

ingredients: 400 g peeled split mung beans, soaked and steamed
500 g pork belly, cut in long strips
2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp sugar
banana leaves, wiped and softened over a flame
steps: Marinate the pork strips with fish sauce, sugar and pepper for 2 hours; mix the drained rice with salt and coconut milk.
Lay banana leaves in a rectangle, spread a layer of rice, then mung bean, a strip of pork, more mung bean and rice, and roll into a tight 30 cm log.
Fold the ends, tie tightly with string every 3 cm.
Boil fully submerged for 8 hours, topping up with boiling water, then drain and press under a weight to cool.
Slice with string and serve with pickled scallions (cu kieu) during Tet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Cu Kieu (Pickled Scallion Bulbs)

ingredients: 1 kg cu kieu (Chinese onion bulbs); substitute small shallots
steps: Trim and peel the bulbs, rub with salt and soak in salted water overnight, then rinse and dry in the sun for 3–4 hours.
Boil vinegar, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves and let cool.
Pack the bulbs and chillies into a sterilised jar and pour over the brine to cover.
Keep at room temperature for 5–7 days until crunchy and sweet-sour, then serve with banh tet and braised pork.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Bo (Steamed Honeycomb Rice Cake)

ingredients: 300 ml coconut milk and 250 ml water
steps: Blend the rice flour, cooked rice and water until smooth.
Warm the coconut milk with sugar until dissolved, cool to lukewarm and whisk into the batter with the yeast.
Cover and rest in a warm place for 4–6 hours until bubbly; add pandan if using.
Oil small cups and preheat them in the steamer, fill three-quarters full and steam on high for 15–20 minutes until springy and honeycombed inside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Da Lon (Steamed Pandan Layer Cake)

ingredients: 300 g tapioca starch and 50 g rice flour
150 g peeled split mung beans, soaked
1 tsp pandan extract or juice of 10 pandan leaves
steps: Steam the mung beans 20 minutes until soft, then blend with 150 ml coconut milk and 100 g sugar.
Mix starch, flour, remaining coconut milk, sugar, salt and 200 ml water; divide in two and colour half with pandan, and mix the other half with the mung bean puree.
Oil a 20 cm tin, heat it in the steamer, then pour in a thin green layer and steam 5 minutes until set.
Add a mung bean layer and steam 5 minutes, alternating until all batter is used, then steam 10 minutes more.
Cool completely before slicing with an oiled knife or string.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Chuoi Nuong (Baked Banana Cake)

steps: Soak the bread in coconut milk and mash smooth, then whisk in eggs, sugar, butter and vanilla.
Fold in two-thirds of the banana slices.
Pour into a buttered 22 cm tin and arrange the remaining slices on top.
Bake at 180 C for 55–60 minutes until set and caramelised on top, then cool before slicing and serve with coconut cream.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Tieu (Hollow Sesame Donuts)

ingredients: 1 tsp instant yeast and 1 tsp baking powder
steps: Knead the flour, sugar, yeast, baking powder, water and oil into a soft dough and rest covered 1.5 hours.
Divide into 12 balls, flatten into 10 cm discs and press one side into sesame seeds; rest 15 minutes.
Fry in 170 C oil, splashing oil on top so they puff up hollow, for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Drain and eat warm, plain or with soy milk.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Cam (Sesame Balls with Mung Bean)

ingredients: 50 g rice flour and 1 boiled potato, mashed
200 g peeled split mung beans, steamed and mashed with 80 g sugar
steps: Mix the flours, potato, sugar and water into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
Roll the mung bean paste into small balls; wrap each in a disc of dough and seal.
Roll in damp hands and then in sesame seeds, pressing so they stick.
Fry in 150 C oil for 10–12 minutes, pressing them gently with a spoon as they puff, until golden and hollow-crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Chuoi (Banana Coconut Tapioca Pudding)

ingredients: 400 ml coconut milk and 300 ml water
2 tbsp roasted crushed peanuts and toasted sesame
steps: Toss the bananas with 1 tbsp sugar and rest 10 minutes.
Simmer water, coconut milk, pandan and the rest of the sugar, add the tapioca and cook 10 minutes until clear.
Add the bananas and salt and simmer 5 minutes until soft.
Serve warm, topped with peanuts and sesame.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Ba Mau (Three-colour Dessert)

ingredients: 150 g peeled split mung beans, soaked
200 g green pandan jelly (agar-based), cut in strips
300 ml coconut milk, 1 tbsp sugar, pinch of salt, 1 tsp tapioca starch
steps: Cook the red beans with 80 g sugar in water for 40 minutes until soft and syrupy.
Steam the mung beans 20 minutes and mash with 70 g sugar and a splash of water.
Simmer the coconut milk with sugar and salt and thicken with the starch.
Layer red beans, mung bean and green jelly in tall glasses, top with crushed ice and pour over the coconut sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Thai (Vietnamese Fruit Cocktail Dessert)

ingredients: 1 can (565 g) lychees and 1 can (565 g) longans with syrup
1 can jackfruit or 200 g fresh jackfruit, sliced
200 ml evaporated milk and 3 tbsp condensed milk
steps: Warm the coconut milk with the condensed milk until blended, then cool and mix with evaporated milk.
Combine the fruits with some of their syrup and the jelly in a large bowl.
Spoon into glasses over crushed ice and pour over the creamy milk.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Khuc Bach (Panna Cotta Jelly Dessert)

ingredients: 6 g agar powder (instead of gelatine to keep it vegetarian)
1 tsp pandan extract and 1 tsp strawberry or matcha powder
steps: Bring the milk, cream, sugar and agar to a boil, stirring, and simmer 2 minutes.
Divide into three portions and colour with pandan, strawberry or matcha, leaving one plain; pour into trays and chill 3–4 hours until firm.
Cut into 1.5 cm cubes.
Serve the cubes with lychees, chilled syrup, ice and toasted almonds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Rau Cau Dua (Coconut Jelly)

steps: Pour out the coconut water and scrape out the flesh; keep the shells if serving in them.
Boil the coconut water with half the agar and half the sugar, stirring, for 2 minutes, pour a layer into the shells or a mould and let set 10 minutes.
Boil the coconut milk with 300 ml water, remaining agar, sugar and salt, pour on top and add slivers of coconut flesh.
Chill 2–3 hours until firm and serve cold, cut in wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sam Bo Luong (Cooling Herbal Sweet Soup)

ingredients: 20 g dried lily bulb or white fungus
steps: Simmer the barley and lotus seeds in the water for 40 minutes until soft.
Add the red dates, white fungus and seaweed and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the longans and rock sugar and cook 5 minutes until dissolved.
Serve warm or chilled over ice as a cooling drink.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bac Xiu (Saigon White Coffee)

steps: Brew a short strong coffee in a phin filter for 4–5 minutes.
Mix the condensed milk and fresh milk in a glass.
Fill with ice and pour the coffee over the milk, then stir; it should be much more milk than coffee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Canh Chua Ca Loc (Sour Snakehead Fish Soup)

ingredients: 600 g snakehead fish (ca loc) steaks; substitute catfish
40 g tamarind pulp soaked in 200 ml hot water, strained
2 stalks bac ha (giant taro stem), sliced, and 1 handful bean sprouts
3 tbsp fish sauce and 2 tbsp sugar
ngo om (rice paddy herb) and ngo gai (sawtooth coriander), chopped
steps: Season the fish with 1 tbsp fish sauce for 10 minutes.
Bring 1.5 litres water and the tamarind liquid to a boil, add pineapple and tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently 8–10 minutes until it flakes, then season with fish sauce and sugar to a sweet-sour-salty balance.
Add okra, bac ha and bean sprouts for 1 minute, then top with fried garlic and herbs and serve with rice and chilli fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Kho To (Clay Pot Caramelized Fish)

ingredients: 600 g catfish (ca bong lau or ca tra) steaks
2 tbsp sugar for caramel plus 1 tbsp sugar
2 tbsp pork fat or vegetable oil
steps: Marinate the fish with fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, shallots, garlic and pepper for 15 minutes.
Melt 2 tbsp sugar in the clay pot with the fat over medium heat until dark amber, then add the fish and turn to coat.
Pour in coconut water, add chillies, cover and simmer on low for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until the sauce is thick and sticky and the fish is cooked through.
Sprinkle with scallions and more pepper and serve in the pot with rice and boiled vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ca Loc Nuong Trui (Straw-roasted Snakehead Fish)

ingredients: 1 whole live-fresh snakehead fish (about 1 kg), uncleaned scales on
1 bundle dried rice straw; or a charcoal grill
20 sheets rice paper and 200 g rice vermicelli
lettuce, herbs, cucumber and green banana
nuoc mam me (tamarind fish sauce) or mam nem
2 tbsp roasted peanuts and scallion oil
steps: Rinse the fish, skewer it from mouth to tail and stand it head down in the ground or lay it on a grill.
Cover with straw and set it alight, adding straw for 20–30 minutes until the skin is charred black and the flesh is cooked through and flaky; on a grill cook 12–15 minutes per side.
Scrape off the burnt skin and scales, place on a platter and top with scallion oil and peanuts.
Wrap flakes of fish in rice paper with vermicelli, herbs and vegetables and dip in tamarind fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau Mam (Fermented Fish Hot Pot)

ingredients: 300 g mam ca linh or mam ca sac (fermented fish)
400 g snakehead or catfish fillet, sliced
water spinach, sesbania flowers, water lily stems and other Mekong vegetables
steps: Simmer the mam in 1 litre water for 15 minutes, mashing, then strain out the bones.
Fry the lemongrass until fragrant, add the strained mam liquid, the stock, eggplant and sugar and simmer 20 minutes.
Bring to the table on a burner and cook the pork, then fish, squid and prawns in the broth for 3–5 minutes until fully cooked.
Add vegetables by the handful and eat with vermicelli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau Ca Keo (Goby Fish Hot Pot)

ingredients: 600 g live ca keo (mudskipper gobies); substitute small loaches or eel
3 tbsp fish sauce and 2 tbsp sugar
1 big bunch la giang (sour leaf), rau dang (bitter herb) and water spinach
steps: Clean the fish with salt to remove the slime, rinse well and season with a little fish sauce.
Simmer stock with lemongrass, tamarind, tomatoes and pineapple for 20 minutes, then season with fish sauce and sugar.
At the table, add the fish (traditionally live) to the boiling broth and cook 8–10 minutes until cooked through.
Add the bitter rau dang and other greens and eat with vermicelli and chilli-salt.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau Ga La Giang (Chicken Hot Pot with Sour Leaves)

ingredients: 2 large bunches la giang (sour Aganonerion leaves); substitute sorrel with a little tamarind
3 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp sugar
500 g rice vermicelli and chilli-salt-lime dip
steps: Season the chicken with half the fish sauce, shallots and garlic for 15 minutes.
Stir-fry the chicken in oil over high heat for 5 minutes until browned, add the stock and lemongrass and simmer 25 minutes until cooked.
Season with remaining fish sauce and sugar; at the table, add handfuls of crumpled la giang, which turns the broth tangy within 1 minute.
Serve with vermicelli and chilli-salt-lime.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lau Ca Linh Bong Dien Dien (Mud Carp Hot Pot with Sesbania Flowers)

ingredients: 800 g ca linh (small mud carp), cleaned; substitute small anchovies or smelt
300 g bong dien dien (yellow sesbania flowers); substitute zucchini flowers
1 bunch water spinach and ngo om
mam gung (ginger fish sauce), to serve
steps: Simmer stock with tamarind, tomatoes and pineapple for 15 minutes and season with fish sauce and sugar.
At the table, add the fish to the boiling sour broth and cook 5–6 minutes until cooked through.
Add sesbania flowers and greens for 1 minute until just wilted.
Eat with vermicelli, dipping the fish in ginger fish sauce; this is the flood-season (mua nuoc noi) dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Mam (Fermented Fish Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 300 g mam ca linh and mam ca sac (fermented fish)
300 g roast pork belly (heo quay), sliced
banana blossom, water spinach, bean sprouts and herbs
steps: Simmer the fermented fish in 1 litre water for 15 minutes, mash and strain.
Fry lemongrass until fragrant, add mam liquid, stock, eggplant and sugar and simmer 20 minutes.
Poach the fish, squid and prawns in the broth for 3–5 minutes until cooked through.
Fill bowls with vermicelli, roast pork and seafood, ladle over the dark broth and eat with the vegetable platter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Nuoc Leo Soc Trang (Soc Trang Khmer Fish Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 500 g snakehead fish, steamed and flaked
3 tbsp prahok or mam bo hoc (Khmer fermented fish); substitute mam ca linh
4 stalks lemongrass and 50 g krachai (fingerroot, ngai bun), pounded
3 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp sugar
bean sprouts, chives, banana blossom and herbs
steps: Simmer the pork bones in 3 litres water for 45 minutes and strain.
Dissolve the prahok in hot water and strain into the broth, add the lemongrass and krachai and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the flaked fish and prawns and simmer 5 minutes until the prawns are cooked, seasoning with fish sauce and sugar.
Serve over vermicelli with roast pork and the raw vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Ca Chau Doc (Chau Doc Fish Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 1 tbsp turmeric powder or 30 g fresh turmeric
bong dien dien (sesbania flowers), water spinach, bean sprouts
steps: Poach the fish in salted water for 8 minutes until cooked, then flake.
Fry lemongrass, krachai and turmeric until fragrant, add the fish and toss 2 minutes.
Add to the stock with fish sauce and sugar and simmer 15 minutes until the broth is golden yellow.
Serve over vermicelli with sesbania flowers and greens, adding roast pork if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bun Ken (Phu Quoc Coconut Fish Noodles)

ingredients: 500 g mackerel or yellowtail fish, steamed and flaked
green papaya and green mango, julienned
steps: Fry lemongrass, shallots and turmeric with the flaked fish for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add stock and coconut milk and simmer 15 minutes, seasoning with fish sauce and sugar.
Put vermicelli, papaya, mango and herbs in bowls.
Ladle the thick coconut-fish broth over the noodles and top with peanuts and chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Hu Tieu My Tho (My Tho Clear Noodle Soup)

ingredients: 30 g dried squid, toasted and 30 g dried shrimp
400 g dried My Tho hu tieu (rice noodles)
200 g lean pork, boiled and sliced
3 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp rock sugar
garlic chives, celery, bean sprouts and fried garlic
steps: Simmer the blanched bones, squid, dried shrimp and daikon in 3.5 litres water for 1.5–2 hours, then season with fish sauce and rock sugar.
Poach the prawns, liver and minced pork in the broth for 3 minutes until cooked.
Blanch the noodles for 15 seconds.
Top noodles with sliced pork, prawns, liver and minced pork, pour over the clear broth and finish with chives, celery and fried garlic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Tam Bi (Silky Rice Noodles with Pork Skin)

ingredients: 500 g fresh banh tam (thick round rice noodles); substitute thick rice spaghetti
200 g bi (shredded pork skin and pork tossed with rice powder)
200 g pork shoulder, grilled with lemongrass and sliced
300 ml coconut cream, 1 tsp tapioca starch, pinch of salt
1 cucumber and lettuce, herbs, bean sprouts
2 tbsp scallion oil and crushed peanuts
steps: Simmer the coconut cream with salt and starch for 3 minutes until thick (nuoc cot dua).
Blanch the noodles in boiling water for 30 seconds and drain.
Put herbs and vegetables in bowls, add noodles, bi and grilled pork.
Top with coconut cream, scallion oil and peanuts, and pour over sweet-sour fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Goi Ca Trich (Phu Quoc Raw Herring Salad)

ingredients: 500 g very fresh sashimi-grade herring (ca trich) or sardine fillets, skinned
1 handful Vietnamese coriander, mint and perilla
4 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, chilli and garlic for peanut-fish sauce
steps: Use only sashimi-grade, freshly caught fish that has been frozen as required for raw consumption; fillet and cut into strips.
Toss the fish in lime juice for 3–5 minutes until it turns opaque white, then squeeze out the juice.
Mix with onion, coconut, peanuts and herbs.
Wrap in rice paper with lettuce and herbs and dip in the garlic-chilli fish sauce mixed with crushed peanuts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Goi Sau Dau (Neem Leaf Salad)

ingredients: 200 g young neem leaves and flowers (sau dau)
300 g ca linh or snakehead fish
200 g pork belly, boiled and sliced
4 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp lime juice
steps: Blanch the neem leaves for 30 seconds to soften the bitterness, then drain.
Grill or steam the fish for 10 minutes until cooked and flake it.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar, lime, garlic and chilli into a dressing.
Toss the neem, fish, pork, cucumber and mango with dressing and top with peanuts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Kho Quet (Caramelized Pork Fish Sauce Dip)

steps: Fry the pork over medium heat for 8 minutes until the fat renders and the pieces turn crisp; add shallots and fry until golden.
Add the dried shrimp and fry 2 minutes.
Add fish sauce, sugar and water and simmer 10–12 minutes until thick and sticky.
Season with pepper and serve as a dip for boiled vegetables and rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Mam Thai (Chau Doc Fermented Fish with Papaya)

ingredients: 300 g mam ca loc (fermented snakehead) from a Chau Doc producer, boned and shredded
500 g green papaya, julienned and dried
steps: Mam thai is made from mam ca loc that is already fermented; buy it from a reputable Chau Doc producer.
Melt the sugar in a pan with 2 tbsp water and cool.
Mix the shredded fish, papaya, garlic, chilli, galangal and rice powder with the sugar syrup and pack into a jar; keep cool for 2–3 days.
Serve with boiled pork belly, rice vermicelli and fresh herbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ba Khia Muoi (Salted Marsh Crab)

ingredients: 1 kg ba khia (small red marsh crabs) from a trusted supplier
steps: Scrub the crabs thoroughly in several changes of water.
Boil the water with salt, cool completely and pour over the crabs in a jar; keep chilled for 3 days.
To serve, remove the shells, crack and mix with lime, sugar, garlic, chilli and papaya.
Serve as a relish with rice; buy ready-salted ba khia from licensed Ca Mau producers if unsure of freshness.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nem Lai Vung (Lai Vung Fermented Pork)

ingredients: 500 g very lean fresh pork leg, finely minced
150 g pork skin, boiled and shredded
3 cloves garlic, sliced, and bird's-eye chillies
guava or chum ruot leaves and banana leaves for wrapping
steps: Nem Lai Vung is a traditional fermented sour pork from Dong Thap, normally bought from licensed local producers; this outlines the method.
Knead the pork with sugar, salt and pepper until sticky, then mix in the pork skin.
Wrap small portions with a garlic slice and chilli in guava leaves then banana leaves and keep in a cool place for 2 days until sour and pink.
Grill the parcels over charcoal for 8–10 minutes until cooked through for safety, and serve with chilli and herbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Cong (Soc Trang Shrimp and Mung Bean Fritters)

ingredients: 150 g rice flour and 50 g wheat flour
100 g peeled split mung beans, soaked
lettuce, herbs and nuoc mam pha
steps: Whisk the flours, water, turmeric and a pinch of salt into a batter.
Season the pork with shallot, scallion and salt.
In a banh cong cup mould, layer batter, mung beans, pork and more batter, and set a prawn on top.
Lower the mould into 170 C oil and fry 8–10 minutes until the cake slides out, then fry free for 3 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
Wrap in lettuce and herbs and dip in sweet-sour fish sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Tet La Cam (Purple Leaf Sticky Rice Cake)

ingredients: 1 bunch la cam (magenta plant leaves), boiled to give purple water
200 ml coconut milk and 1 tsp salt
300 g peeled split mung beans, steamed
300 g pork belly, in strips, marinated with fish sauce and pepper
sweet fish sauce with shredded coconut, to serve
steps: Soak the drained rice in the la cam water for 2 hours until purple, drain and mix with coconut milk and salt.
On banana leaves, layer rice, mung bean, pork and egg yolk, more mung bean and rice, and roll into a tight log.
Tie firmly every 3 cm and boil submerged for 6 hours, topping up with boiling water.
Cool under a weight, slice and serve with sweet fish sauce with coconut.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Pia (Soc Trang Durian Pastry)

ingredients: 300 g plain flour for the water dough plus 150 g for the oil dough
120 g vegetable shortening (instead of lard, to keep it eggetarian)
300 g peeled split mung beans, steamed and mashed
150 g sugar and 3 tbsp vegetable oil for the filling
6 salted duck egg yolks, steamed and halved
steps: Cook the mung bean, durian, sugar and oil in a pan over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring, into a thick paste; cool and roll into 12 balls around a half yolk.
Make a water dough of 300 g flour, 70 g shortening, sugar and water, and an oil dough of 150 g flour and 50 g shortening; rest 30 minutes.
Wrap oil dough in water dough, roll out and fold twice to make flaky layers, divide into 12, wrap each filling ball and flatten slightly.
Bake at 180 C for 15 minutes, brush with egg yolk and bake 12–15 minutes more until golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Banh Bo Thot Not (Palm Sugar Sponge Cake)

ingredients: 200 g palm sugar (duong thot not), melted with 150 ml water
2 tbsp toddy palm fruit flesh, pureed (optional)
steps: Mix the rice flour with the coconut milk, cooled palm sugar syrup, palm puree and salt.
Stir in the yeast, cover and ferment the batter 6–8 hours until bubbly.
Oil a 20 cm tin, heat in the steamer, pour in the batter and steam 25–30 minutes on high until risen and springy.
Cool and cut into wedges; serve with grated coconut.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Keo Dua Ben Tre (Ben Tre Coconut Candy)

ingredients: 500 ml thick coconut cream from fresh Ben Tre coconuts
150 g malt syrup (mach nha) or glucose syrup
1 tsp pandan extract or 1 tbsp cocoa (optional flavours)
edible rice paper sheets for wrapping
steps: Combine coconut cream, sugar and malt syrup in a heavy pan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 35–45 minutes until very thick and pulling from the sides (about 120 C).
Stir in the butter and any flavouring.
Pour onto an oiled tray, smooth to 1.5 cm and cool until firm but still pliable.
Cut into small bars and wrap each in rice paper then waxed paper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Che Buoi (Pomelo Sweet Soup)

ingredients: pith (white inner peel) of 1 large pomelo
100 g peeled split mung beans, soaked
300 ml coconut milk with a pinch of salt
steps: Cut the pomelo pith into small cubes, knead in salted water and squeeze several times, then soak 1 hour, changing the water, to remove bitterness.
Squeeze dry, coat the cubes thickly in tapioca starch and boil 3 minutes until translucent, then cool in water.
Steam the mung beans 20 minutes; simmer 1 litre water with sugar and pandan, add the mung beans and pomelo and thicken with a little starch slurry.
Serve warm or cold with the salted coconut milk poured on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Nuoc Thot Not (Toddy Palm Juice)

ingredients: 500 ml fresh toddy palm sap (nuoc thot not), freshly collected; substitute canned palm juice
200 g young toddy palm fruit flesh (cui thot not), sliced
steps: Use the sap fresh on the day it is collected before it starts to ferment; it is a sweet, non-alcoholic drink.
Strain the sap through a fine cloth.
Pour over ice with slices of the soft palm fruit, sweeten with palm sugar syrup if needed and serve chilled.
